books/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campa.text: # I — THE WORLD AND CAMPAIGN **THE CROWN · The Returned Ark** **v1.1.1 · Table edition · Year 1200, Recall Day 21** **Marshall Alexander** The Crown hangs over its old capital. Five thousand people live among its gardens, workshops and broken streets. Above them, the murdered king walks in borrowed flesh. His daughter waits in the highest tower. **At the table:** I holds the campaign, capital, history and encounters; **[II — Areas](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md)** holds the places and their exits; **[III — Ways](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md)** holds journeys and repairs; **[IV — People, Monsters and Treasure](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md)** holds identities, profiles, magic and finds. Numbers identify localities; route IDs identify the connections between them. ## Contents [Writs and buyers](#writs) · [Hearths and frontiers](#territorial-overview) · [Expedition procedure](#world-procedure) - [The Return](#world-opening) - [Marrbridge and the shore pointcrawl](#world-capital) - [Life aboard](#world-living) - [The Crown Annals](#world-chronology) - [Evidence, rumours and old papers](#world-knowledge) - [The first force](#world-army) - [The invasion: referee reference](#world-truth) - [Odelia Marr and the royal inheritance](#world-royal) - [Campaign procedure](#world-procedure) - [Footholds and companies](#bases) - [Regional encounters](#encounters) - [The named Custodians](#custodians) - [Endings](#world-endings) [I · Contents](#contents) ## The Return Three weeks ago, at morning court in Marrbridge, the Necromancer murdered King Edmund Marr. Pale cords left a failing human disguise and entered his still-warm body. Wearing the dead king, it seized Princess Odelia Marr and raised his bloody hand towards the empty sky. The Crown appeared between two heartbeats. Wind broke windows along the harbour. Its shadow crossed six bridges, the cathedral and the palace rock. Bells answered from streets three thousand six hundred metres high. A stone platform descended to the river, received the king's body and his captive daughter, and rose into the cloud. The first rescue force went up and broke in the growing country. Survivors now sell damaged armour beneath the granary arches. The regent and Parliament have opened the treasury to anyone who can finish the work. Begin at **[2, Granary Ward](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-2)**. Read the proclamation. Describe the impossible city above the river and the boat crews working beneath it. Ask what the company wants, what it can carry, and whom it trusts to take it aboard. Old collections, fallen soldiers' equipment, spell books, precious materials and creatures worth seeing offer reasons to climb. A boat and tested chain cradle join **[3](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-3)** to **[1](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-1)**. Beyond Rootgate, local knowledge soon gives way to guesses. ### The proclamation > **BY THE REGENT AND PARLIAMENT OF MARRBRIDGE** > > Six hundred pounds shall be paid for Princess Odelia Marr brought home alive and free. > > One hundred and fifty pounds shall be paid for the identifiable remains of King Edmund Marr. > > Two hundred and fifty pounds shall be paid for the lasting destruction of the Necromancer. > > Each award stands upon its own accomplishment. Any person or company may claim it before Chancellor Katherine Harcourt at the Palace Stairs. Bring witnesses and what proof can be carried. > > **The sums are reserved. The treasury will honour them.** | Accomplishment | Award | |---|---:| | Odelia Marr returned alive and free | £600 0s 0d (144,000d) | | Edmund Marr's identifiable remains recovered | £150 0s 0d (36,000d) | | The Necromancer permanently defeated | £250 0s 0d (60,000d) | **Payment.** Odelia Marr can identify herself. Marshal Margaret Marr and the palace surgeons examine her brother's remains. Lasting defeat requires the destroyed heart, defeated sophisticated manifestations and the final parasite killed or securely sealed; see [IV, the organism](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#organism). Direct witnesses and the physical aftermath can establish the claim. Chancellor Katherine Harcourt hears disputed evidence and pays the separate awards. A company can begin at once, owing its swords to whomever it chooses. [I · Contents](#contents) ## Marrbridge and the shore pointcrawl Marrbridge occupies the river mouth beneath the old imperial anchorage. Some 180,000 people crowd its walls and port suburbs. Stone quays support timber houses whose upper floors almost meet across the lanes. Six bridges divide the river traffic; bells count the opening of their gates. Foundries smoke below the palace rock. Students argue on the cathedral steps while porters shoulder grain past them. The Crown is one ancient cylindrical ark-city: about **3,600 metres high and up to 1,000 metres across**. Its mineral Frame bears human streets, homes, gardens, cisterns and great works. Gravity within is ordinary. Sunlight reaches inward from outer courts and roof openings; vast interiors need carried light. The coast is warm, with wet seasonal winds. A sheltered gulf receives the estuary; grain plains and upland pasture feed the city. The Crown's lowest sill hangs **42 metres above mean river level**. Its printed heights rise from that sill: the summit is more than three kilometres above the harbour. The city above moves on its own ancient supports; the old roads and utility joints end in open air. These eight shore points give the company a small familiar world beneath the ascent. **A and B are existing Areas 2 and 3.** The other letters identify shore neighbourhoods described here. A first visit or a substantial transaction takes one Turn. The listed connecting streets are included; familiar travel follows the ordinary rule of up to three points in a Turn. Boat and hoist journeys use their stated times. ![Marrbridge shore pointcrawl: eight connected neighbourhoods and the working route to Rootgate.](maps/THE_CROWN_Shore_Pointcrawl.svg) | Point | Connections | What brings adventurers here | |---|---|---| | **A · Granary Ward (2)** | B, F, H | Beds, stores, hirelings, equipment and buyers. | | **B · River House (3)** | A, C, E | Boat passage, cradle watches, loading and casualties. | | **C · Fish Stairs** | B, D, G | Fishing crews, small boats and a clear view of the lower hull. | | **D · Shipwright Reach** | C, E | Rope, carpenters, floating stages and boarding projects. | | **E · Old Root Pier** | B, D | Broken imperial approaches, old anchor seats and exposed salvage. | | **F · Palace Stairs** | A, G, H | Royal witnesses, the regent, proof and payment. | | **G · Cathedral Close** | C, F, H | Treatment, burial, annals and news from returning companies. | | **H · West Bridge Exchange** | A, F, G | Parliament, militia hiring and merchants able to buy a great haul. | ### A · Granary Ward — Area 2 Four storeys of granary arches face the southern quay. Beneath them, soldiers sell dented helmets beside men selling rope by the fathom. The proclamation has been pasted over an older notice about spoiled flour. **Beatrice Holt [independent capital trade; [P01](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P01)]** keeps the Unfallen Door. Pay for a bed, leave a locked chest, and tell her who should receive it if the company fails to return. **Daniel Ward [independent capital trade; [P01](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P01)]** buys portable finds at the adjoining scale. He has **£80 0s 0d (19,200d)** available each week; larger introductions lead to H. Ordinary equipment priced up to **£10 0s 0d (2,400d)** per item is available. City smiths can complete larger ordinary commissions in two days when their stock and the equipment rules permit. Four porters, four soldiers and one surgeon are presently seeking work. Prices and quarters appear under [Footholds](#base-2). **Follow:** the covered grain lane to B; the steep palace road to F; the bridge market to H. ### B · River House — Area 3 An old ferry hall stands on piles beside the disconnected utility collars. At each cradle bell, people look up from their drinks to count those coming down. **Oswald Talbot [independent capital trade; [P02](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P02)]** keeps boats, weather watches and a chalk loading board. Across the water, **Joan Mercer [Lower Carrying / Rootgate; [P02](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P02)]** answers from Rootgate. **[FC001](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-FC001)** takes one Turn each way: eight people with packs, or a patient with three attendants, within its **1,000 kg live-load limit**. Passage costs **£0 0s 1d (1d) per person**; patient and three attendants together cost **£0 0s 2d (2d)**. Dangerous crosswind suspends the watch. Waiting boats stay beneath the tower only while their crews can hold position. The boat landing and the Crown's chain cradle are separate pieces of work. Losing a boat or breaking a brake has an immediate, visible consequence. Joan Mercer arranges casualty extraction when the company sends an agreed signal. **Follow:** the grain lane to A; the tide steps to C; the old stone embankment to E. ### C · Fish Stairs Fish scales silver the steps. Nets hang between shrine posts; gulls watch the gutters. From the lowest landing, the empty Barn Rail joint at **6** is visible against the sky. Someone has painted its outline on a shed door and drawn three different ways to reach it. **Captain Ellen Rook [Parliament / river watch; [P05](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P05)]** works here during the morning landing, then makes the harbour round. She wants boats clear of falling tackle and will lend an experienced coxswain to a well-prepared casualty run. Fishing crews can report which Crown winches moved that day and where a boat could lie beneath them. A hired small boat gives access to the underside and a view of possible anchors. Establish its crew, load and return signal before leaving. The Crown's fishing tackle can become another entrance once someone reaches and secures its upper machinery. **Follow:** quay steps to B; the net walk to D; the fishmongers' lane to G. ### D · Shipwright Reach Hull ribs stand in the mud like cattle at a trough. Mallets answer from open sheds. Long poles above the roofs carry flags marking gusts under the Crown. **Edith Barlow [Lower Carrying / Works; [P06](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P06)]** trades drawings with these yards through boat crews; she normally works aboard at **6/28**. Bring her a measured sketch of a Crown anchor, brake or missing panel. The shipwrights can quote for rope, tackle, a floating work stage, a gangplank or replacement timber. Their products must still reach the upper fixing. Hire ordinary carpenters or riggers at **£0 1s 0d (12d) per day**, plus materials and board. A sound shore workshop lets the company prepare a difficult job, store bulky finds and recruit enough hands to carry them. Major machinery uses the projects in III. **Follow:** net walk to C; the towpath beneath the old rails to E. ### E · Old Root Pier Twelve centuries of masonry meet at this pier: dressed imperial stone, patched flood walls, a warehouse foundation built over an old rail. Overhead, the matching ends of roads and pipes hang clear of the river. Water falls from one blind flange each time a Crown cistern spills. The old approaches remain **[RR173](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR173), 2–1; [RR174](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR174), 2–6; [RR175](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR175), 3–11; and [RR176](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR176), 3–7**. Their missing central spans prevent through passage. Their shore mouths are reached through A or B; this pier gives a useful view of the joints and access for survey boats. **Boarding projects.** A line secured from above can lift a ladder or a light gangway. A tested winch can lower a boat or cradle. A properly founded stage can receive heavy salvage. Inspect both anchors, establish the gap and rated load, then obtain tackle and a working party. Use the surviving route's clearance and support limits once restored. Improvised rope access has its own declared load and fall protection. The work can give the company a lasting second entrance. **Follow:** embankment to B; towpath to D. ### F · Palace Stairs The palace rises from a rock threaded with stair streets. The king's empty bier stands in the lower chapel. Petitioners pass it on their way to the treasury; the guard has stopped trying to keep flowers off the steps. **Marshal Margaret Marr [Royal house; [P44](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P44)]**, the king's sister and acting regent, wants her niece home and her brother buried. She can equip a credible rescue, supply family testimony and bring an armed escort into play. She needs a route and arrangements for governing during her absence. Parliament's order presently keeps her ashore; she obeys while arguing for an expedition. **Chancellor Katherine Harcourt [Joint treasury; [P06](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P06)]** receives claims in the lower hall. Her deputy at A can arrange a hearing. Bring witnesses, recovered remains, an account of the heart's destruction, or a living princess. Palace surgeons assist with identification and ordinary treatment. **Follow:** palace road to A; chapel lane to G; upper bridge street to H. ### G · Cathedral Close Sun falls through the cathedral's broken western glass onto beds borrowed from its school. Bandages dry between the cloister pillars. Beneath the bell tower, a clerk copies the names of those who returned. Surgeons treat at **£0 1s 0d (12d) per day**, plus board and consumed supplies. Funeral crews receive identified remains; the chapter keeps copied annals of the departure and the Crown's rare later sightings. Returned soldiers leave accounts here because their families know where to ask. Ask for the *Departure Book*, the names crossed out on the first-force roll, or the most recent witness to Odelia Marr. The chapter can provide texts and introductions. Actual spells and their Sources appear at their keyed locations in IV. **Follow:** fishmongers' lane to C; chapel lane to F; scholars' walk to H. ### H · West Bridge Exchange Parliament sits among the old wool scales. Merchants wait under painted guild signs while messengers carry petitions through the weighing doors. From the gallery, the Crown seems balanced on the bridge roof. **Speaker Thomas Hales [Parliament; [P06](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P06)]** controls the treasury vote and city militia. He wants reliable intelligence, an evacuation road and enough public authority to survive the discovery of a flying royal fortress. He will finance useful reconnaissance and preparations for another force. His supporters disagree over salvage claims and the regent's powers. Assayers and merchant syndicates can collectively buy up to **£400 0s 0d (96,000d)** in a week. A greater sale brings several buyers to the same table or divides payment across weeks. Their scales, escorts and carts make an enormous find worth recovering. **Follow:** bridge market to A; upper street to F; scholars' walk to G. ### A week beneath the Crown A survivor auctions a route sketch; a new cradle awaits its upper anchor; a funeral closes the fishmongers’ lane; Parliament funds a survey boat; a glazier offers labour for a captive colleague; a windshift reveals a shaded opening. ## Three optional writs Three desks stand beneath the public proclamation at **Marrbridge’s Palace Stairs**. **Katherine Harcourt** records a company’s representative and shares. Sign any writ without fee. A unique discovery or rescue pays once to the first accepted claim; collaborating companies may share it. Return people, goods, witness testimony or a usable drawing as evidence. The clerk publishes accepted routes at Granary Ward. Surveying an already posted road earns nothing. ### Plumb, Rule, and Compass > **The Masons, Surveyors and Enginewrights of Marrbridge** pay the company below for dangerous new roads and restored conveyances within the Returned Crown. Bring a usable account of both approaches, carrying limits and what you changed. Unclaimed salvage remains yours. We ask first opportunity to buy technical manuscripts; you may refuse our price. > > Company ____________________ Representative ____________________ > > Signature ____________________ Date __________ Clerk __________ **Edith Barlow** advises the Palace Stairs desk; **£600** reserved. New dangerous connecting route **5s**; first release of a hidden return **£2**, including its survey; actionable bank-repair plan **£5**, credited toward restoration. Completed lower/local banks, H, Orchard or Rain Stair **£15**; upper passenger, freight, water, garden, Harvest or Beacon works **£30**. An independently rigged second shore entrance, proven with an unmanned load, earns **£40** once. Reserve a named project’s payment before employing its crew. A measuring kit, tackle and 100 ft of rope can be borrowed against a **£3** bond; other costs belong to the company. ### Salt and Sepulture > **The Cathedral’s Last Wash** pays the company below for the missing, safe burial and destruction of the works that bind our dead. Bring names where they can be learned. Bring the living to care. The dead are received for burial; known personal effects are offered to their families. > > Company ____________________ Representative ____________________ > > Signature ____________________ Date __________ Clerk __________ **Constance Byrd** advises Cathedral Close; **£600** reserved. Identification and location of a posted missing person **2s**, credited toward recovery. Safely returned identified remains **10s**; a difficult upper carry can be commissioned for **£2**. Each living resident captive rescued earns **£2** and immediate treatment. Permanent destruction of the five centres earns: **lower ganglion £35; curing works £50; upper warning link £75; grafting stock £100; Heart £50**. The printed opening rolls define the personal claims; ancient unnamed remains need an agreed recovery fee. Treatment kits, salt and cloth may be advanced against the payment. A company-created casualty earns no bounty. ### Muster and Recovery > **The Marshalcy of Marrbridge** pays the company below for our living people, lost service stores and roads by which the wounded can come home. Record names and circumstances faithfully. Known personal effects remain with their owner or family; unrelated unclaimed salvage remains yours. > > Company ____________________ Representative ____________________ > > Signature ____________________ Date __________ Clerk __________ **Margaret Marr**, through **Ellen Rook** at the River House; **£800** reserved. Each of the 52 living royal personnel aboard returned freely to agreed care earns **£2**, or **£4** when carried on a litter. Serviceable missing arms are bought at an inspected price. North Light’s signal book and one corroborating account earn **£10**; the three scouts at 183 returned with their diary earn **£10** beyond their rescue fees. A staffed casualty road through 136, both landings secured and a return proven, earns **£40**. Repairing machinery, opening a road and saving people are different achievements and can earn separate awards. Funds are reserved as jobs are accepted; further work needs announced backing. Public rewards remain **£600 for Odelia Marr alive and free, £150 for Edmund Marr’s identifiable remains, £250 for lasting defeat of the Necromancer**. Those require no signed writ. ### Buyers and opening offers | Interest and contact | Offer and support | |---|---| | Merchants · **Daniel Ward**, Granary Ward | Buys bullion, gems and art. His own £80 weekly purse is supplemented by assayers and syndicates; inspected large lots can reserve £2,500 over a fortnight. Secure storage and staged auctions. | | Armourers · **William Bennett**, through Granary Ward | **£6** for a measured rubbing of the Black Chimney Sword at 71; repairs and fits one recovered armour piece with the report. Ordinary arms bought on inspection. | | Engineers and shipwrights · **Oswald Talbot**, River House | **£8** for a demonstrated plan of the Folding Stair at 209, returned to the company. Boats, test loads and storage for another way aboard. | | Glaziers · **Alexander Rallis**, through the shore desk | **£6** for a complete rub and tested dimensions of the old lens mounting at 164; protective crates and two carrier-days. | | Physicians · **Florence Chaddock**, Cathedral correspondence | **£5** for the labelled healing observations in 184’s weather chest; treatment, sample vessels and an interpreter of wound signs. | | Scholars · **Robert Fawcett**, Palace Stairs desk | **£10** for a complete copy of the dynastic diagrams at 91, with access agreed by its keeper. Five days’ workroom and copying materials. | | Seedkeepers · **Alice Atwood**, Fish Stairs correspondents | **£3** each for viable abandoned whitebean, skywheat or copperpea lines at 169, 179 or 196; pots and a cultivator for the descent. Respect the tended planting stock. | | Collectors · **Constance Byrd**, Cathedral Close | **£20** for a drawn record of the newly exposed garnet setting at 39a. A conservator appraises art and arranges buyers. | The private commissions reserve **£100**, separate from purchase funds. Known households retain their property. Unclaimed ruins and enemy hoards can be plundered; their objects’ claimants, when any, appear in the key. Agree price and transfer before surrendering a large lot. [I · Contents](#contents) ## Life aboard The Crown carries streets built by people who expected their children to use them. Arcades have become houses; roofs have become orchards; a theatre still raises its curtain above a town grown between the columns. New timber sits on old stone. A replaced window may be younger than its owner, while the hand that opens it has worked there for a thousand years. Five communities keep separate wells, kitchens, schools, workshops and customs. Their reliable paths join a small part of the tower. Beyond the last swept threshold, a sound building can be utterly dark. Rain grows a forest through one roof while a sealed room beside it preserves its painted walls. | Community | People on its roll | Hearth and ordinary circuit | |---|---:|---| | Lower Carrying | 1,870 | **47**; kitchens, stores, water and care at 20/34/36/52/55. | | Arena | 950 | **84b**; ovens, hospital and civic stores around 74/77/80. | | Lantern | 1,140 | **128**; school, clinic, fire court and water at 132/135/139/144. | | High Seed | 730 | **198**; protected draw, seed houses and dry returns around 192/196/197/199. | | Crown Watch | 334 | **214**; roof stores, emergency water and the summit's sheltered walks. | The opening roll totals **5,024 living people aboard**. It includes displaced households, visitors, living captives and the surviving members of the royal expedition. The first-force account below locates the soldiers separately. These are community rolls; a visit to a hearth finds the people currently working, resting or sheltering there. ### The ration clerk's slate At 74, Speaker Matilda Vernon keeps the five communities' figures beside the latest route reports. The present shortfalls belong to the damaged crops, interrupted work and current anchorage of Recall Day 21. **Food.** About 143 hectares remain planted across 300 hectares of growing bays; managed woodland occupies a further 65 hectares, partly overlapping the old gardens. This season's worked plots, woods, fish, ponds and fungi supply the equivalent of 1,157 dry tonnes a year for people, against 1,206 tonnes planned issue. The 49-tonne annual gap follows abandoned plots, displaced growers and broken carrying routes. Restoring their use changes the next harvest. Rotating stores hold 228 dry tonnes; six tonnes of shore grain have arrived since Return. The Dragon's annual levy of 72 wet tonnes of fish is recorded separately from human issue. **Water.** Protected cells hold 88,600 m³: 48,000 lower, 26,500 middle and 14,100 high. Another 6,200 m³ await treatment or assay. At this anchorage, with damaged collector branches, average capture is 505 m³ daily against 580 m³ makeup. The 75 m³ daily shortfall draws on reserves until capture improves or use falls. A freed dry inspection gallery gives access to repairs; clean cell lids, isolation valves and living crews determine which water can actually be drawn. **Power.** Wind supplies 0.33 MW, solar work 0.20 MW and water head 0.04 MW: about 0.57 MW against 0.48 MW of priority demand. Five MWh of storage and 19 tonnes of reserved fuel support three electrical islands. Cables, motors and staffed watches deliver that power. The burned freight machinery at 136 still needs its own parts and labour. **Boats and materials.** Eleven fishing hulls are ready; three are being refitted at 6. Crews now sound the changed shoals beneath the capital. Rope, baskets, tile, mortar, timber hulls and simple tools are made aboard. Fine bearings, large panes and particular electrical fittings fetch good prices. A carried replacement can restore more useful work than a sack of coin. These pressures give inhabitants something to ask for and adventurers something valuable to change. Use a named damaged place and its consequence when the situation worsens or improves. ### Air, light and growing country Two journeys cross each other throughout the Crown: upwards into colder, thinner, more exposed air; inwards from sunlit walls into deep darkness. A warm outer orchard can share a height with a dry black vault. Shelter stops wind and rain; altitude remains. | Country | What travellers notice | |---|---| | Marine rim, roughly 0–300 m | Salt on iron, warm drains, boat bells, wet stone and sudden crosswinds. | | Lower city and gardens, roughly 300–1,100 m | Orchard light, household smoke, shade beneath old roofs, warm abandoned works. | | Belfry forests, roughly 900–2,200 m | Wet bark, hidden roofs, dripping canopy, sudden shafts of sun across enormous voids. | | Cloudwood, roughly 2,000–2,900 m | Mist, moss, wind in narrow gaps, slick branches and long cold interiors. | | High works and Crown, roughly 2,900–3,600 m | Hard light, chill stone, fierce exposure, low vegetation and precious dry rooms. | Widow Pear, First Bell and Cloud Ladder are individual great trees with roots, crowns and crossings at addresses. Their branches hide buildings and shade productive ground. Human treads have been renewed on some limbs; other limbs belong to climbing animals. Ash-lace feeds on accumulated litter and dead timber. Sparse luminous patches reveal themselves; carried light reveals footing. ### Beasts with their own lives **Bell-Under**, at 15a, has a 7.4-metre carapace and a 19-metre deployed reach. Its feeding bank and deep moult refuge lie in brackish water. The shed shell is a find with a living owner nearby. Little gutter crabs inhabit narrower reaches. At 144 a great freshwater cephalid waits below the den lip, reaching for whatever comes close enough to seize and drag. Small pocket cuttle inhabit other pools. At 153 a person-sized mantle-newt blends with wet tile; its slime companion remains a separate body capable of surviving alone. Rabbit-sized cloak-bats carry fruit and seeds into their roosts. Masktails climb with dexterous hands and prehensile tails, stealing food and testing latches. Boughcats stalk those same approaches. Roofbacks browse fallen growth. Case-building siltwright larvae alter small watercourses with stone, fibre and ceramic grit. Spiders occupy high broken fabric. Centipedes follow warm trenches and abandoned drains. Fungal beetles pull wet timber apart. Find their silk, cast skins, waste, feeding heaps and routes. A creature's hunger or defence of its young can make passage dangerous. Watch how it lives to find a method that works. ### The Dragon's descendants The lineage develops from a hooded, limbless skyserpent into a legless winged wyvern, a rear-legged winged drake, and a four-legged winged young Dragon. Mature Dragons are rare; the Great Dragon is exceptional. Reproduction begins among young Dragons. Their large clutches meet predation, hunger, dispersal and the hazards of the tower. Venom thickens towards burning secretion. A segmented rattle carries electrical force. A knot of mating bodies may resemble a hydra: each animal still has its own body, wounds and actions. Some 580 lesser forms occupy their recorded ranges. **Mélusine** remains the one established fully mature resident, grown Great in the long centuries since her arrival. She remembers people whose names survive only on objects in her hoard. The lesser creatures hunt, nest, quarrel and leave according to their own needs. Mélusine wants Odelia Marr. The princess's beauty, royal inheritance and possible Dragon form have revived an old appetite for possession. At 213c the receiving crew can carry a specific offer. The Dragon may protect a road, spare a person, give treasure, or take a hostage according to the bargain made. Her body and magic make every meeting consequential. ### Hearths and frontiers The five communities hold inhabited circuits rather than whole bands of the tower. Roofed streets end at bolted doors; water and work may survive beside an enemy-held hall. Read the named entrance when crossing a divided locality. | Community | Hearths and working circuit | Beyond its protection | |---|---|---| | **Lower Carrying** | 20, 47, 52; boats, workshops, water and family courts | Wet culverts, the mortuary road and unlit upper tenements. White Widow uses 39–42–35–47–44–55–59–66–93–99. | | **Arena** | 74, 77, 84b; council, hospital, theatre and markets | The north cleft at 80, west stand, hanging houses and Pear pump at 99. | | **Lantern** | 128, 132, 150; food, rope, hospice and school | The six at 136 face the dead army. Above, spiders and the curing works at 156 control the returns. | | **High Seed** | 198; seed houses and clean draw reached through 196 | Rain Court 194, northern 195 and 199’s cargo apron; keepers hold the southern tap and inner wicket. | | **Crown Watch** | 214 and the defended 208–212/215–216 galleries | The king at 206, Heart at 207 and prison 217; Mélusine holds 213a–b beyond the receiving court. | A lasting clearance, repaired gate and supplied watch can turn a wild route into a maintained one. Refuge meals, lamps, spare hands and secure storage make that victory useful to the next company. ![Hearths, contested approaches and principal ascents.](maps/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_Strategic_Overview.svg) [I · Contents](#contents) ## The Crown Annals *Copied from the Departure Book, the seed-house rolls, the navigators' books and the receiving accounts. Robert Fawcett keeps the dry collection at 83; copies of the early leaves also survive in Marrbridge Cathedral Close. Marginal hands record the objects and practices that outlasted their makers.* ### Before the departure **Year −1.** The aboard roll counted 28,800 people. Trains ran beneath Rootgate; the garden cages carried workers among 300 planted hectares. Schools, baths and markets kept their hours. King Roland Marr and the navigators watched the northern light called Lucifer from the Instrument Garden. The city was still joined to its capital. **Two days before the Fall.** Observers disagreed over the light's course. Their readings went to the king, Council and rail offices. Water crews rehearsed the refuge doors. Shops stayed open. **Year 0, Day 0.** At six hours and twelve minutes a white light broke in the north. Nine minutes later the paving shivered. The northern telegraph stations ceased answering. Copper light filled the sky. The Crown and the capital stood. **Days 1–3.** Trains and carts brought the northern survivors. Fire ran through the capital's eastern quarter. Crown crews opened wards, carried water and helped the shore brigades. Fine grit settled on the northern roofs; the Rain House turned the first dirty water aside. **Days 4–7.** A grit squall tore the north collector mesh and fouled the high freight drive. On the seventh day Esther Dorr sealed a northern sample. Pale points shone when she closed the lamp shutter. Filaments in the glass turned briefly against the sampling wheel. She signed the wax and kept the vessel apart. **Days 8–12.** Council allotted cots, grain and medicines in the Forum. Glaziers reopened the Upper Clinic ramp screen by the twelfth day. Washed roofs began admitting rain again after assay. **Days 13–16.** Mabel Fell carried three living graft lines in separate clean trays. A produce run waited for them. On the fifteenth day a summit rescue party, caught between weather doors, followed cold light from rivet to rivet until it reached the manual refuge ring. Council ordered departure in stages and left a stocked clinic and archive copies ashore. **Day 18.** Adela Venn admitted a late hospital carriage and struck a machine crate from the loading board. Its parts went to the shore clinic. At dusk King Roland Marr, the navigators and Rootwrights released the roots. The shore ledger was copied to the Forum. The bronze board kept the altered order until its surrender in Year 169. **Days 19–40.** The Crown went southwest and waited upon the weather. Assayed maritime rain entered the cells. Fuel dynamos served the essential watches. Families took borrowed rooms; schools taught in shifts. The fortieth-day roll counted about 39,800 aboard. Crews were still repairing the northern mesh and freight drive. ### The first generations **Days 41–120.** At Tideglass Estuary 6,100 went ashore with two barges and pump tools. At Lantern Bight 4,900 left with a hospital delegation and glass stock. At Stone-Reed Harbour 3,600 took seed, pilot boats and guides. Adela Venn entered their receiving places. Some later letters came back. **Months 5–12.** A further 14,200 joined existing settlements ashore. At the first year's end about 10,500 remained aboard, with 630 dry tonnes of food in store. Stone-Reed boatwrights taught the sheltered descent. The first fishing trial followed the anniversary of departure. **Year 2.** A bitter fall stained the north collector. Esther Dorr's crew saved the covered drinking cells and lost an opened nursery run. **Year 3.** The upper freight drive was recoupled. In these years crews renewed northern mesh, made separate brine pans and replaced two baggage tracks with boat cradles. By the end of Year 5, some 8,200 people remained aboard. **Years 6–18.** The flotilla grew to twenty-four boats. A visiting crew brought a Tideglass letter: families still lived there, though new toll lords divided the inland road. Beside other names the clerks wrote, *No answer*. **Year 11.** Three workers escaped the drying-house fire. Witnesses counted a fourth figure opening the inner latch. **Year 14.** Cloaked figures stood in the storm cloud level with the Bell Terrace. Its bell rang while tied. King Roland Marr and the navigators turned away. The fishing interval was lost; the boats came home. **Year 20.** A trickle began beside exposed Foundation stone at the Seed House. One graft entered as dead put forth a bud. The keepers measured the water and returned that graft to the living list. **Year 26.** Roland Marr laid down the stewardship after supervising Blanche Marr's training at the hand hollows. Council witnessed her accession. **Year 42.** Roland Marr died. In these decades Mabel Fell also died, having seen descendants of the three grafts she carried out of the capital. Her death year has worn from the leaf. **Years 35–50.** Some ministries closed. The foundry ceased its great castings; smaller forge work, schools and hospital continued. The cold line returned to the refuge ring, and another hand copied the account beneath the first. **Year 50.** Blanche Marr authorised surveyed fair-weather sea holds. Navigators entered the soundings and the conditions for departure. **Year 60.** Blanche Marr and Council governed about 8,900 people. Cultivation, boats, schools, care and repairs continued. New clerks learned to copy the old measures before taking their own. **Year 72.** Geoffrey Marr was born. **Years 96–129.** Workers opened the dry seed return, now [LS002](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-LS002). Veilwings nested outside the east cloud screen. **Year 104.** One hundred people joined existing households at Birch Inlet. Timber and clay were exchanged for salt and repair work. **Year 119.** A reed consignment from South Marsh carried mirror-newt eggs into the isolated pond. Their descendants are still tended there. **Years 130–167.** Geoffrey Marr learned Council, Navigation and Balance work. He practised his compact Dragon form at 92 and his holds at the hand hollows. Their names precede the battle roll. ### The coming of Mélusine **Year 168.** Mélusine landed during a recovery watch, already heavy with eggs. The gunners tore her left wing; Geoffrey Marr drove her from the ready court. She broke the canopy and forced the aircraft store. Bridget Rell's gunners held the Battery while Geoffrey Marr defended the apron. Blanche Marr was wounded at Navigation. She kept the broken side leeward until the last evacuees passed the fire door and the last passenger cage cleared. Her witnessed words were: *Keep the door for those behind you.* She died after the rescue. Geoffrey Marr survived with a burned shoulder. Empty hooks remained in the audience hall; wooden cups replaced silver in the Instrument Garden. Mélusine laid 250 eggs. **Year 170.** Two hundred and five skyserpents hatched. They climbed the packing stacks, entered roof joints and descended outside. Forty-five eggs failed. **Years 169–171.** The receiving screens and walled returns were completed. Through the following six years the young spread into summit cavities, the signal roof, collector lee racks and stepped gardens. Households screened their doors and returned captured strays at the receiving court. **Year 175.** Seventy members of craft families accepted invitations from Red Quay households. Clay, fibre and scrap came aboard in exchange. **Year 180.** Geoffrey Marr and Council governed about 10,020 people. Mélusine lived in the two chambers. Of the first hatchlings, 130 remained: 100 skyserpents, 25 wyverns and five drakes. Sixty had died after hatching; fifteen had left the Crown. ### The heir in the Dragon's house **After Year 180.** Three lean harvests ate into the reserve. Travellers climbed the remaining stages. **Year 321.** Christina Marr asked for her son's supervised practice at the Motive, with guards and a promise of return. Mélusine refused. **Year 327.** Christina Marr made the staged summit ascent before the west storm. [I · Contents](#contents) ## The invasion: referee reference ### The dead king and the Recall Edmund Marr died in the palace. Occupation destroyed his nerves and living royal faculties. The Necromancer wears his body, borrows fragments of memory and speaks through white cords in his opened throat. His death is final under the campaign's restoration magic. The princess knows because she saw it happen. His dead royal tissue touched an ancient homeward recognition in the Frame. The Crown returned. During that response **[FC009](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-FC009)** carried the king and gear, 90 kg; Odelia Marr and gown, 60 kg; the discarded disguise, 60 kg; and a sealed larval burden, 10 kg. The **220 kg load** rose on an **800 kg tray** from 1 to 215. The platform now rests there, inert. A trained living bearer can recover its primordial action through the hand hollows. ### The five centres Pale roots join five occupied works: the lower ganglion at **99**, curing trays at **156**, warning link at **195**, grafting stock at **206** and Heart at **207**. Roots carry speech and warning immediately; bodies and detached messengers travel through the Ways. Cutting a link leaves the isolated guards on their last orders. The complete procedures for bodies, living invasion, cleansing, centre attacks, the royal graft and the Rain are together in **[IV, The organism](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#organism)**. Its centre table gives what each loss changes. Keep that chapter open when the company confronts the infestation. ### Finite bodies At Recall Day 21, **160 mature bodies** serve the infestation: 32 royal dead, 16 recently killed residents, 64 old human bodies and 48 animals. The twelve bodies carried from 39 belong to the old-human total. Three corrupted Collectors and the occupied king are separate. Twenty-four secured royal corpses remain available for short-lived raw animation; they belong to the 71 unmatured dead. Twelve colonies of larvae complete the opening stock. The complete current distribution, equipment and guard reserves appear in **[IV, Force ledger](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#force-ledger)**. Move these bodies when orders and routes allow. A patrol drawn from a gate leaves fewer guards at that gate. Equipment follows its body, and ammunition is spent. Fresh dead need access, preparation and the times printed in IV before they can reinforce a formation. ### The royal project The Necromancer wants a living royal bearer who can deliberately command the Motive. Odelia Marr has the inheritance and still needs to learn its use. Her captor uses threats, a stolen father's tenderness and promises about other captives to obtain purposeful cooperation. At Recall Day 21, the fine grafting work has yet to begin. Stock waits below, the Signal Stair is broken, and the captors still seek instruction. The project will leave things to find: requested instruments, clean linen carried upward, new restraints, a missing tutor and practice marks at the controls. Prisoners can smuggle appeals or bargain for one another. Use **[IV, The royal project](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#royal-project)** to date preparation, interruptions and the invasion itself. ### The Rain The Rain is a human gravity-bombardment work: **207 stores ammunition; 206 loads the fall well; 8 holds the lower shutters and inspection interlocks**. Its tube runs between them. The lower Crown Watch post can hear work in the shaft and watch the shutter dogs. At the opening, the cradles are empty and the lower shutters are dogged shut above Marrbridge. Ammunition, crews, repaired handling gear and an opened well would turn the old work against the city. Their movements give the company something to discover and attack. [I · Contents](#contents) ## Odelia Marr and the royal inheritance **Princess Odelia Marr [Royal house; [P07](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P07)]** is eighteen, with copper hair and sea-blue eyes. At 217 a bronze chain reaches the window, books, stove and one loose floor tile. She has a stabilised Grave Wound, a concealed pin and a clear memory of her father's murder. Her dagger and notes lie under the tile; her war chest stands beyond the chain. Her bird messages and care for another captive have already helped the rescue. She asks first about the wounded below. House Marr descends from a magical union of Dragon and Man. Living bearers can awaken the ancient recognition and assume Dragon form. Royal command joins that inheritance to conscious intent and learned control. A blood touch can reveal recognition; the hand hollows require a mind capable of choosing and maintaining a hold. ### The change Freed, healed to **Serious or better**, and shown or credibly taught her inheritance, Odelia Marr may choose her young-Dragon form, **[P45](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P45)**. Margaret Marr's family account, the portraits at 83 or 91, The Waiting One, Mélusine or her own responsive blood and scales can provide the understanding. Bring her to a place with room for the body and wings printed in IV. Above the summit arches, her copper hair becomes a line of bright scales. Sea-blue eyes look back from an unfamiliar face. The chain, laid on the stone, is suddenly very small. Her memory, wounds and judgment persist. She can address the Motive and hold the present anchorage. With charts, hand hollows and instruction, she can choose a nearby verified sea hold or a slow departure into favourable conditions. A successful lesson can also reopen the Recall Cradle. Keep the learned command and conditions on her record so the achievement remains useful. ### The regent **Marshal Margaret Marr [Royal house; [P44](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P44)]** wears armour and governs in her brother's place. Her inherited recognition can wake certain primordial thresholds and draw a Custodian's attention. She needs the same practical instruction before attempting strategic navigation. Parliament presently keeps her ashore; a negotiated escort, an emergency or open defiance can bring her into the Crown. The aunt and niece can cooperate, quarrel and learn from one another. A conscious royal bearer can command under coercion. Protecting a bearer therefore means protecting her freedom, teachers, companions and route to the controls. Odelia Marr can restore the house, share power, decline a throne or leave with people she trusts. Love, marriage and shared rule can grow from her choices and relationships. Returning her alive and free fulfils the rescue award. Her life afterward belongs to the story made at the table. ## Expeditions and the light A Crown Turn is **thirty minutes**. An unfamiliar ordinary approach and destination take one Turn; deliberate investigation takes another. Cross up to three successive familiar ordinary passages in one Turn, rounding the run up when it ends. An exceptional Way costs its printed journey Turns, plus one exploration Turn at an unfamiliar arrival. Resolve combat, treatment and short magic in their own minutes within that time. **Exposure.** Once per active Turn, check the highest risk of the ground the company used: **secure refuge 0; maintained road 1-in-6; abandoned ground 2-in-6; wild, contested or enemy-held ground 3-in-6**. Count both approach and destination on an unfamiliar ordinary move. A familiar run uses the highest of its crossed passages. Locate the event on that ground; reaching a safe door does not erase the approach. An exceptional journey uses its route risk. Quiet rest inside an expressly defended refuge is secure. Ordinary Ways inherit the higher endpoint risk unless their card gives another rate. The rate covers exposed exploration, not every room behind a defended inner door. A cleared passage improves when its gate, watch, lighting and supply are maintained; mark its new risk beside the changed route. **Events.** Each key lists eligible numbered rows from its regional table. Roll uniformly among that short list: use the next larger die and reroll excess faces. Signs, aid and contact need not become fights. Use Surprise, distance, Reaction, Morale and pursuit when uncertain. Fixed occupants and traps act when their circumstances trigger, regardless of a wandering roll. A known alarm response replaces the routine roll for that interval; immediate gunfire attention still resolves promptly, without charging another Turn. **Persistence.** A travelling patrol leaves its parent garrison with its equipment. Mark losses and important movements; reaching a meeting requires an open route and elapsed time. Unique creatures and hoards exist once. Removed loot, destroyed bodies, opened doors and completed repairs stay changed. A depleted encounter leaves its aftermath; common wildlife and weather may recur. Significant new occupation follows a neighbour’s movement or a visible enemy undertaking. **Light.** BRIGHT permits detailed visual work; DIM shows shapes and movement; DARK supplies no useful ambient vision. In GEWINN, sight-dependent Attacks, Checks and AC Saves against a located target take [–] in darkness; an unlocated target may make the action impossible. A torch lights **30 ft for 60 minutes**, an oil lantern **20 ft for 240 minutes**. A dark lantern gives a 20-ft cone; a bull’s-eye gives a 60-ft cone. Each occupies a hand while carried. One fill is one Slot; one Burn represents twenty minutes alight. Extinguishing pauses fuel; a shuttered flame still burns. Source ranges stop at opaque doors, corners and cover. Keep a reserve and a means of relighting. Lighting, shuttering or setting down a lamp costs an Action under pressure. Lanterns withstand ordinary wind and rain; a dropped lit vessel suffers Wear, and a Ruined one spills oil. An ignited spill deals 1d6 Burning. Visible light betrays its bearer beyond the illuminated pool. Spiders read connected silk; water creatures feel nearby ripples; hunters use hearing, scent and their own sight. **Shared campaign.** Before departure, record company, objective, starting refuge, date, supplies, hirelings and proposed return. Characters may finish at an established upper refuge and begin their next expedition there. A session ending in danger pauses that company until withdrawal is resolved; absent characters remain with it or can be replaced by characters already at the next departure base. On return, treat wounds, count recovered goods and remaining fuel, pay wages, settle claims and update the shared map. Resolve overlapping expeditions chronologically. Date important caches, vacancies, sightings and opened routes. Between journeys, advance an enemy undertaking, a rival expedition and a local consequence only as their people, routes and elapsed time permit. Food, carriers, repair crews and refuge beds come from the places supplying them. A great find can alter a company’s standing, obligations and plans. Windfalls can change a company’s ambitions. She can provide soldiers, equipment, testimony and a royal command learner. A credible route and governing arrangement can bring her aboard. **Parliament.** Thomas Hales holds money and militia support. He seeks evacuation capacity, defensible public authority and control of the capital's exposure. Reliable maps, a second entrance and proof of the enemy's means strengthen a request for aid. **The five communities.** Matilda Vernon speaks for households whose needs sometimes conflict. Waterkeepers, growers, nurses and machinists control much of the labour an expedition needs. They want occupied branches cleared, damaged work restored and people returned. Protection of a local custom can buy more trust than a royal seal. **The survivors.** Jocelyn Markham wants the remaining people found and his maps used well. Recovered equipment, a cleared freight bay and a sound casualty road can make his camp an ally for another advance. **Mélusine.** The Great Dragon wants Odelia Marr and guards her two chambers, tribute and possessions. Either offers a brief chance to communicate. | [I · Contents](#contents) ## The named Custodians **282 primordial cores remain; thirty-six workers have folk names.** Human hands renew their timber, cloth, wire and fittings. Their closed cores endure through repairs that can no longer reproduce them. Each has an old task, a routine and a material need. A Custodian helps through that task. Watch its movements, bring the required tool or prepare a safe place for its load. Repeated work can turn familiarity into trust. Warnings precede the ordinary dangerous movements described below. A damaged body may be isolated or repaired; a broken core is a lasting loss. **Profiles:** [P13](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P13) for ordinary workers; [P14](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P14) for heavy work. Each entry gives its profile. Most stand 1.75 m and weigh 170 kg; differing bodies are stated. Carry the Custodian's weight as well as its burden when testing a route. [I · Contents](#contents) ## Endings Resolve each accomplishment when it happens: the princess freed, wounds healed, inheritance understood, remains recovered, heart destroyed, final parasite killed or sealed, navigation learned. Pay each earned award. Let people describe what the company has changed. **Above the cloud.** Odelia Marr steps into open sky and chooses her Dragon form. She can carry hope back into the city, learn to move the Crown and decide whom to trust. Rescue may end the campaign here. A defeated heart and final parasite can make it a lasting victory over the invasion as well. Love and shared rule can follow a freely chosen relationship. **A restored house.** Odelia Marr accepts the throne and uses learned command to hold or move the Crown. Margaret Marr and Parliament negotiate government ashore. The five communities retain their homes, institutions and practical power, subject to the settlement actually made. The company's repaired works and property remain useful. **A public settlement.** Parliament funds supply routes and manual works. Odelia Marr accepts a navigation mandate, retires or negotiates another place in government. A humane settlement can bring stability and relief. Coercive custody creates enemies among the same people it confines. **The Dragon's house.** Mélusine receives Odelia Marr under a bargain or seizes her. A bounded agreement may protect lives; possession gives the Dragon a powerful hostage. The princess can bargain, resist, learn or escape. Apply the words agreed and the people able to enforce them. **A stolen command.** An enemy compels a living royal bearer to make an effective command. The Crown becomes a moving stronghold for that enemy. Its journeys, occupied dead and human weapons follow their preparations. The capital has time to act when those preparations give warning. The princess's death or destruction of her person is a loss, with the remaining powers and conflicts carried forward. **A fortune and a road home.** The company frees captives, recovers treasure, improves an entrance and leaves. Their friends, claims, enemies and unfinished business remain. The uncommanded Crown may hold its anchorage or resume wandering when conditions make it leave. After any ending, the arcades still smell of cooking. Predators hunt the abandoned works. A newly repaired cage rings for its first load. The company can close the book or return to a changed city.

books/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md.text: # II — The Areas *The Crown, Year 1200. The opening position is Recall Day 21.* Each numbered key covers one traversable locality: a court and its workrooms, a garden bay, a shared residential lane or a bounded stretch of a giant tree. Its **extent** states the ground included. Within that ground, use the described doors, screens, levels and sightlines. A named person stays with the locality or expedition recorded for them until events move them. Crown and Skyworks](#chapter-10) — 206–217 ## Reading the keys The first paragraph gives light, air and sounds at the threshold. Daylight follows the sun and fails at night; a stated lamp is a local source whose reach ends at the next screen, bend or distance described. Open galleries feel the weather. A carried light reveals what lies within its actual reach. **Height.** The z figure is the Crown's structural datum. During this hold, add 42 m for height above the estuary. Shore keys use their own ground. Dimensions follow the current physical structure; the regional plans locate whole localities and their connecting ways. **Time.** One Turn is thirty minutes. Exploring an unfamiliar ordinary locality costs one Turn; deliberately searching it costs another. Cross up to three successive familiar ordinary localities in one Turn, rounding each continuous run up before exceptional movement. An exceptional Way costs its listed journey Turns; add one exploration Turn only for an unfamiliar arrival. Repairs, exposure, spells, treatment and combat keep their actual durations. Full procedures and service intervals are in [Book III](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#travel). **Local cards.** GEWINN quick profiles give **STR/INT/FTH/WLL**, movement, AC, DR, action and Morale. Physical DR is **Slashing / Piercing / Bludgeoning / Shot**; other resistances are named. S/P/B abbreviate those damage families. Common people and Custodians use the [front reference](#quick-reference); creatures and dangerous unique people have cards beside their key. Book IV supplies complete special procedures and spell references. A card describes the listed body; counts and current weapons come from the key. The final brain-squid and a chosen Dragon change appear only when their stated conditions occur. **Finds and ownership.** £1 = 20 shillings = 240 pence; 1 shilling = 12 pence. Every find lists value and packed Slots. Worn equipment uses its own worn load. A reward, shop price or loan remains the offer described. Record removed objects, ammunition, rescued people, severed tissue and repaired passages. Changes persist. **Encounters.** Use the named regional table in Book I at the normal check, keeping the actual occupants, open approaches and passed barriers in play. A roaming Collector or named beast has one recorded position. A local encounter can move a present creature into the company's path; record its departure from the former position. **Reading exits:** An unqualified route is open and ordinary: one Turn to explore an unfamiliar destination, up to three familiar passages in a Turn. Printed T values are exceptional journey times. Special restrictions and loads are shown; III gives every surveyed width and headroom. Unqualified human paths admit packs; carts and carried litters are marked. Risk is the exposure chance in six; the full procedure is in I. Neighbours use P01, growers and mechanics P02 unless an individual profile is given. ## Common people and Custodians These profiles cover ordinary working equipment. The injuries, weapons, tools, ammunition and worn gear listed in each key determine what that person has now. The local role and Reaction govern how they use it. ### P01 — Neighbour / porter **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 10/10/10/10; Move 35 ft. AC 2; DR 3/2/2/0; club: 1d4 B (5 ft). ML 6. Club handling [–]; flees a lost fight. ### P02 — Grower / waterkeeper **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 12/12/10/12; Move 40 ft. AC 2; DR 3/2/2/0; work knife: 1d4 S (5 ft). ML 7. Protects crops and valves; knows one neighbouring route. ### P03 — Watch / hired guard **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 14/10/10/12; Move 35 ft. AC 10; DR 11/7/6/5; spear: 1d8 P (5 ft) or crossbow: 1d10 P (20–300 ft; Reload 1 Action). ML 8. Crossbow: stow shield (AC 6; DR 9/5/5/5), Reload 1 Action. ### P04 — Crown gunner **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 14/12/10/14; Move 35 ft. AC 7; DR 11/6/5/5; musket: 3d8 Shot (30–400 ft; Reload 3 Actions) or hanger: 1d6 S (5 ft). ML 8. Musket Reload 3 Actions; six shots. ### P05 — Veteran / company leader **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 14/12/12/14; Move 30 ft. AC 12; DR 12/10/7/5; spear: 1d8 P (5 ft) or arbalest: 2d8 P (30–800 ft; Reload 2 Actions). ML 9. Arbalest: stow shield (AC 8; DR 10/8/6/5), Reload 2 Actions. ### P06 — Scholar / clinician **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 10/14/12/12; Move 35 ft. AC 2; DR 3/2/2/0; club: 1d4 B (5 ft). ML 7. Treatment tools and four dressings; club handling [–]. ### P13 — Standard Custodian service chassis **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 16/14/10/16; Move 40 ft. AC 11; DR 10/8/6/4; hand or integrated work arm: 2d6 B (5 ft) or security halberd/tool, where actually fitted: 2d8 P (10 ft). ML 10. Made; one fitted attack or STR 16 Control; directive and visible controls govern work. ### P14 — Heavy Custodian chassis **GEWINN:** STR/INT/FTH/WLL 18/12/10/16; Move 35 ft. AC 12; DR 12/10/8/6; bracing or stone work arm: 3d6 B (8 ft) or integrated drill/cutter, where actually fitted: 2d8 P (10 ft). ML 10. Made; STR 18 Control; Grave drive injury halves Move, a second immobilises. ![The Crown: vertical section](maps/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_Vertical_Section.svg) ## 1 — Arrival and root interfaces ![Regional plan: Arrival and root interfaces](maps/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_Region_01.svg) ### 1 — Root Ramp and Departure Gate *Rootgate · z 0 m · working harbour; rescue landing* **Risk 1** · **Light / air:** BRIGHT at the seaward sill; DIM beneath the canopy; DARK galleries above. Berth lamps at night; salt spray and answering launch bells. **Extent.** 100 × 60 m. The limestone ramp hangs forty-two metres above the estuary. A chain cradle descends beside the salt pans. Four empty bronze mounts surround a wooden board painted FINAL TRAIN. **[Joan Mercer](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N007) — Lower Carrying, fishing and stretcher crews; [P02](#quick-P02)** directs the landing. Eleven fishing hulls are ready; three are under repair at **[6](#node-6)**. Fishing boats bring news and equipment from the lower expedition camps. The crews know the fishing water and Rootgate; their maps thin out beyond the inhabited streets. **Boarding.** The basket from **[3](#node-3)** carries eight people with packs, or a patient and three attendants. Each cradle has its own brake. [Joan Mercer](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N007) arranges extraction when a shore party signals; high wind suspends launches. Lash passengers and cargo before crossing the sill. An unsecured person caught by a swinging basket must make a STR Check or fall into the estuary; secured passengers strike the sill but remain attached. **The painted board.** A line copied beneath FINAL TRAIN names **Adela Venn — ancient boarding gatekeeper**: “Day 18. The hospital carriage went first.” Its original bronze board survives at **[213a](#node-213a)**. **Ways out** | Destination · Way | Journey / passage | |---|---| | [2 Granary Ward](#node-2) · [RR173](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR173) | detached shore approach; cart/litter; 2,000 kg | | [3 River House](#node-3) · [FC001](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-FC001) | 1 T; weather exposed; eight packs or a wheeled patient with three attendants; 1,000 kg combined | | [4 Visitors’ Gate](#node-4) · [RR163](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR163) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [5 Customs Arcade](#node-5) · [RR001](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR001) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [6 Rail Throat](#node-6) · [LD030](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-LD030) | people and sealed fish handcarts | | [9 Quarantine](#node-9) · [RR096](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR096) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [19 Grease Court](#node-19) · [RR236](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR236) | litter; 100 kg | | [35 Grain Exchange](#node-35) · [RR192](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR192) | 1 T; litter; 100 kg | | [35 Grain Exchange](#node-35) · [RR207](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR207) | 1 T; heavy freight; 6,500 kg combined | | [215 Motive Gallery](#node-215) · [FC009](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-FC009) | inert; Tray 3 m wide × 2.5 m clear height; 800 kg combined | **Encounters:** [Rim](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#region-Rim) 1/2/3/4/5. ### 2 — Ground Harvest and Forest Exchange *Root Dependencies · shore · Marrbridge market ward; expedition base* **Risk 0** · **Light / air:** BRIGHT through the granary arches; lamps under reed roofs and after dusk. River damp, turnips and hot tallow. **Extent.** 120 × 80 m. Limewashed sheds and a tented buying yard crowd the ancient exchange shell. Beyond the granary foundations, woodland climbs the edge of Marrbridge. The Unfallen Door's sign hangs beneath an arch taller than the tavern. **[Beatrice Holt](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N008) — independent innkeeper; [P01](#quick-P01)** rents beds, storage and a back room for hiring. **[Daniel Ward](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N009) — independent recovery broker; [P01](#quick-P01)** buys Crown finds. The Crown's sill hangs forty-two metres overhead; its severed utility collars now serve as mooring rings. A burned military boat lies hauled beside the boatwright's shed. **[Oswald Talbot](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N010) — independent boatwright; [P02](#quick-P02)** fits cradle brake shoes while his crew moves timber and stretchers. Its old ground cables and dynamos are gone. **Investigate.** An abandoned litter bears the royal household's crown mark. Failure drops the frame on the nearest worker for 2d6 Bludgeoning. This is **shore point B** on the [Marrbridge pointcrawl](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#world-capital). Boats, stairs and towpaths connect it with the other shore neighbourhoods. **Finds** - **[T50](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#treasure-T50) — Burned boat bronze.** £3 0s 0d (720d); 16 Slots; Salvage. Faded districts end in blank stone; fresh charcoal stops at broken lift banks. **Lucy Ashby [Rootgate watch; [P03](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P03)]** admits armed travellers and sells her lower map for 1d: Rootgate, Works Ward, Lower Market and their connecting roads. Yard lamps at night. Salt draughts enter through root doors; a slow iron knock repeats below. **Extent.** 100 × 80 m. Anchor chains vanish beneath carved survey stones. A patched timber yoke rests across **Old Yoke — autonomous Custodian; [P14](#quick-P14)** as workers cut cradle brake blocks. A child's breakfast stall stands immediately outside the chalk sweep. **Crossing.** Deep wheel grooves cut the way through the yard. Wet straw and carbolic soap; a man pleading, “Keep my arm.” **Extent.** 95 × 80 m. An older animal ramp cuts diagonally across the washable court. Green-glazed drains lead to a sealed wash pit. Inspectors move along the raised gallery, above the patient floor; a separate ramp takes cleared patients out. **[Philippa Sewell](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N015) — Lower Carrying clinical workers; [P06](#quick-P06)** holds a resident bedding porter's dressing open. Pale larvae move inside an open Grave wound. He is conscious. Hot instruments, clean dressings and restraints lie ready.
