Cold air stops at the massive shutters; the isolation bay has its own vent. **Extent.** 90 × 60 m. **Andrew Hext — Crown Watch; [P06](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P06)** tends seven injured residents; twelve Watch rotate duty. **White Porter — Custodian; [P13](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P13)** carries one casualty and litter. **Shutter Man — Custodian; [P13](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P13)** warns before operating the marked closures. Bleeding gets immediate care. Treatment 1s daily; bed 1d or work; food 3d daily. Stores hold **eighteen guest-days**. Armour loan: **£2 bond or a returned patient**. The upper chain wheel releases **RR206’s** jammed leaf, widening its **1.2 m gap to 1.4 m**, with 2.3 m headroom. Cover its rooted floor for casualty passage. The water-crew cage is still disabled. An old leaf records rescuers following cold light to the manual ring after the Fall. Another names **Christina Marr**, who died here two days after her **327** storm hold. These wheels still protect routes to **208–211 and 216**. **Waiting for a return.** Two of Andrew Hext’s seven patients were wounded in Bourne’s Day-16 attempt on the prison. Eighteen guest-days of food are available: six visitors for three days. The watchers ask for a withdrawal signal before lending their litter. **Ways out** | Destination · Way | Journey / passage | |---|---| | [195 High Cistern](#node-195) · [RR206](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR206) | 7 T; contested; 195 defended south approach; 1.2 m-wide side gap; release from 214; Packs and carried litter; stairs 1.4 m wide × 2.3 m high; current shutter gap 1.2 m wide; 450 kg combined party, litter and gear per flight/rest bay | | [195 High Cistern](#node-195) · [RR230](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR230) | service; disabled; 195 south water-crew landing; 214 interlock and feeder; cart/litter; 500 kg combined | | [208 Crown Arrival](#node-208) · [RR095](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR095) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [209 Sky Rigging](#node-209) · [RR090](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR090) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [210 Navigation Hall](#node-210) · [ER022](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-ER022) | cart/litter; 1,200 kg | | [210 Navigation Hall](#node-210) · [RR135](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR135) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [211 Aircrew Court](#node-211) · [DP007](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-DP007) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [215 Motive Gallery](#node-215) · [RR136](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR136) | litter; 100 kg | | [216 Crown Battery](#node-216) · [RR153](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR153) | cart/litter; 500 kg | **Encounters:** [Crown](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#region-Crown) 1/2/3/4/9. ### 215 — Motive Interface Gallery *Crown and Skyworks · z 3,450 m · kept Motive gallery; spent Recall cradle and broken beacon stair* **Risk 1** · **Light / air:** DARK gallery lit by three human lamps. The hand hollows are warm; weight and distance press through the bones before language. **Extent.** 80 × 55 m. **The Waiting One — Custodian; [P13](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P13)** waits beside the warm hand hollows. A dark stain marks the couch touched by **Edmund Marr’s occupied body — Royal house; [P08](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P08)** on Day 0. The spent Recall cradle rests here; the worker witnessed its homeward movement. Living royal capacity, deliberate intent and learned handling govern the Motive. The Waiting One teaches a freed bearer to hold, open a Frame gate or attempt controlled translation. This broad floor admits **Odelia Marr’s** chosen Dragon form and practice. The stair to **217** has a deliberate **twelve-metre break**, made on Day 2. Four masons and twelve days complete **Beacon / RR088**. **FC010** climbs exposed staples for four Turns to a narrow hatch. Drinking draw and ordinary drain remain separate from the Motive. **Quick profiles** - **[P07](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P07) — Odelia Marr, captive princess (if brought here).** G 14/18/14/16; Move 30 ft. AC 0; DR 0/0/0/0; ruby-hilted dagger, if recovered: 1d4 P (5 ft). ML 10. Great typed Wounds; stabilized Grave Piercing WV 7, thirsty; hidden pin reaches shackle. - **[P45](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P45) — Odelia Marr, young Crown Dragon (if she changes here).** G 18/18/14/16. AC 8; DR 7/5/3/2; Shocking 8; bite: 2d8 P (10 ft) or talons: 2d6 S (5 ft) or Crown Breath: 2d8 Shock (30 ft). ML 11. Great typed Wounds, no Huge; Fly 80 ft; 12m long/3m folded; breath recharge d6=6. **Ways out** | Destination · Way | Journey / passage | |---|---| | [1 Root Gate](#node-1) · [FC009](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-FC009) | inert; Tray 3 m wide × 2.5 m clear height; 800 kg combined | | [212 Balance Court](#node-212) · [RR087](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR087) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [214 Crown Refuge](#node-214) · [RR136](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR136) | litter; 100 kg | | [217 Sky Signal Tower](#node-217) · [FC010](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-FC010) | 4 T; contested; packs; hatch 0.8 m wide × 1.5 m high; 150 kg on the climbing line. A rigid litter will not pass | | [217 Sky Signal Tower](#node-217) · [RR088](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR088) | 1 T; broken; litter; 100 kg | **Encounters:** [Crown](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#region-Crown) 1/2/3/4/10. ### 216 — Crown Garrison and Battery Gallery *Crown and Skyworks · z 3,450 m · Crown Watch battery; six gunners and twelve cannon rounds* **Risk 1** · **Light / air:** BRIGHT battery arches; DARK southern elbow, crew lamps at night. Cold wind, oiled steel and a shielded eastern lobby. **Extent.** 90 × 70 m. Six **Crown Watch gunners** hold one repaired light cannon and **twelve rounds**. Their barriers protected the evacuation to **214**. A manual shutter faces **207’s** occupied magazine. **RR150’s masonry elbow screens the Heart.** A shot requires moving and re-emplacing the gun or opening a straight line, with muzzle clearance, recoil space and sound support. Opening the magazine shutter also exposes the crew. **LS001** reaches the aircrew house behind its fire screen; **RR153** reaches the refuge. The gunners lend a pavise and Worn cuirass for casualty rescue. The Rain at **206** has separate loading work and lower interlocks. **Cannon:** 4d10 Shot, useful range 30–600 ft; GEWINN WLL attack, no STR handling, outside-range Attack and Damage [–]. Three crew aim/fire, swab and load; four sequential Reload Rounds require all three duties. Interrupted rounds make no loading progress. **Ways out** | Destination · Way | Journey / passage | |---|---| | [207 Mycelial Heart](#node-207) · [RR150](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR150) | contested; cart/litter; 2,000 kg | | [209 Sky Rigging](#node-209) · [DP006](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-DP006) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [211 Aircrew Court](#node-211) · [LS001](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-LS001) | cart/litter; 500 kg | | [213 Flight Apron](#node-213) · [RR148](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR148) | restored; cart/litter; 500 kg | | [214 Crown Refuge](#node-214) · [RR153](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR153) | cart/litter; 500 kg | **Encounters:** [Crown](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#region-Crown) 1/2/3/4/9. ### 217 — Sky Signal Tower *Crown and Skyworks · z 3,462 m · highest beacon prison; four guards and a living royal captive* **Risk 3** · **Light / air:** BRIGHT high balcony by day; DIM rotunda beyond the blue shutters. A guarded stove and lamp at night; DARK stair bend. Bronze chain scrapes stone. **Extent.** 65 × 50 m beacon rotunda, attached balcony and roost braces; floor z 3,462 m, gable about 3,486 m. **Princess [Odelia Marr](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N002) — Royal house; [P07](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P07)** is eighteen, copper-haired, with sea-blue eyes. A bronze chain runs from the window pier far enough to reach the stove, books and one loose floor tile. It stops short of both doors and the cedar war chest. She watches the guards, then turns toward an unfamiliar footstep. **Her work.** Beneath the tile she has hidden a ruby-hilted dagger and notes of the guard changes. She also keeps a concealed pin within reach. She feeds birds, has helped a worker escape and has tied white-and-blue signs visible from **[211](#node-211)**. During a distraction she can jam the inner bolt. She asks first about the wounded below. **The guard.** Four mature occupied halberdiers retain coat-of-plates armour and morions. Two watch the intact **[209](#node-209)** stair; two rest beneath the screened beacon platform. A guard striking the stair rail wakes the resting pair in this same rotunda. A contained larval basket waits beside a locked worktable. **Free and heal her.** Proper cutting or lock tools free the chain in one Turn; combat and urgent treatment use their actual durations. She is dehydrated and has one stabilised **Grave Piercing Wound, WV 7**. The chest holds Worn royal harness, a longsword, **£0 8s 0d (96d)** and **two Healing draughts, [M01](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#item-M01)**. Her concealed dagger and these stores comprise **[T_U17](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#treasure-T_U17)**, her property. **Choose the escape.** The intact rigging stair, repaired beacon stair, exterior stapleline or a valid aerial approach can bring rescuers here. Balcony arches are **4 m wide**; the separate loading slit is **0.75 m**, the staple hatch **0.8 m**. The **18 skyserpents and 10 wyverns** roost outside the screened lower roof and move independently of the guards. **The change.** Once free, informed and healed so every Wound is Serious or better, [Odelia Marr](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#contact-N002) can choose her first Dragon form as a d4 Action. Her **12 m body, 3 m folded width and height** fit the rotunda and broad balcony. Equipment falls where she changes; her mind, injuries, memories and loyalties remain hers. **[T40](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#treasure-T40)**, the signal master's silver case, is a separate **£80 0s 0d (19,200d)** one-Slot find. The tools, companions and route the rescuers secured determine what they can carry away together. **Quick profiles** - **[P07](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P07) — Odelia Marr, captive princess.** G 14/18/14/16; Move 30 ft. AC 0; DR 0/0/0/0; ruby-hilted dagger, if recovered: 1d4 P (5 ft). ML 10. Great typed Wounds; stabilized Grave Piercing WV 7, thirsty; hidden pin reaches shackle. - **[P10](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P10) — Mature Necromite / infested soldier.** G 14/3/0/10; Move 30 ft. AC 5; DR 8/5/4/2; four halberds 2d8 S at 10 ft, or grasp/bite 1d4 P at 5 ft. ML 12; Dead, Turning HD 2. - **[P12](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P12) — Grave-larvae / exposed necromite colony.** G 3/1/0/4; Move 10 ft. AC 1; DR 0/0/0/0; Open-wound contact: 1 Tox Damage per 30 minutes; see invasion. ML 4. Salt/reaching wash clears surface patch in one Action; deep cleansing 10 minutes. - **[P15](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P15) — Skyserpent.** G 8/3/0/10; Move 35 ft. AC 6; DR 2/1/1/0; bite: 1d4 P (5 ft) or spit: 1d4 Tox (15 ft). ML 6. Downward glide; venom WLL Defense avoids, renews after meal +1 hour. - **[P16](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P16) — Wyvern.** G 12/5/0/12; Move 40 ft. AC 8; DR 4/3/2/1; bite: 1d6 P (5 ft) or rattle discharge: 2d4 Shock (5 ft). ML 7. Fly 60 ft; one rattle/hour with food; WLL Defense avoids Shock. - **[P45](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#profile-P45) — Odelia Marr, young Crown Dragon (if she chooses the change).** G 18/18/14/16. AC 8; DR 7/5/3/2; Shocking 8; bite: 2d8 P (10 ft) or talons: 2d6 S (5 ft) or Crown Breath: 2d8 Shock (30 ft). ML 11. Great typed Wounds, no Huge; Fly 80 ft; 12m long/3m folded; breath recharge d6=6. **Finds** - **[T40](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#treasure-T40) — Signal master's silver case.** £80 0s 0d (19,200d); 1 Slot; Unclaimed. A palm-sized silver casket set with eight small sapphires rests in the old signal keeper’s recess. Its padded interior held a lens, now missing. One Slot; £80 to a collector of imperial instruments. Opening the recess needs its ordinary lock picked, forced or released from the inside. - **[T_U17](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#treasure-T_U17) — Odelia Marr's war chest.** £33 6s 4d (7,996d); 22 Slots; Held. Her ruby-hilted dagger **£8 0s 0d (1,920d)**; Worn royal harness **£21 10s 0d (5,160d)**; longsword **£1 5s 0d (300d)**; wool cloak **£0 3s 4d (40d)**; cash **£0 8s 0d (96d)**; and two Kindly draughts [M01](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md#item-M01), **£2 0s 0d (480d)** together. Twenty-two Slots packed. The dagger and observations are under the loose tile; the chest stands beyond her chain. Odelia Marr owns and chooses how to use or lend these things. - **The old signal clasp.** A sapphire-set clasp is trapped in the former signal keeper’s desk, separate from Odelia Marr’s property. £2 10s 0d (600d); 1 Slot. **Ways out** | Destination · Way | Journey / passage | |---|---| | [209 Sky Rigging](#node-209) · [RR089](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR089) | 1 T; contested; barred shutter; 0.75 m loading slit; Odelia Marr’s loose bolt; packs; 450 kg party, litter and gear per flight/rest bay | | [213 Flight Apron](#node-213) · [DP014](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-DP014) | animal way; young creatures as described; 0.8 × 1 m | | [213 Flight Apron](#node-213) · [RR147](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR147) | broken; cart/litter; 500 kg | | [215 Motive Gallery](#node-215) · [FC010](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-FC010) | 4 T; contested; packs; hatch 0.8 m wide × 1.5 m high; 150 kg on the climbing line. A rigid litter will not pass | | [215 Motive Gallery](#node-215) · [RR088](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md#route-RR088) | 1 T; broken; litter; 100 kg | **Encounters:** [Crown](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#region-Crown) 1/2/3/4/5/10.

books/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md.text: # III — THE WAYS *THE CROWN v1.1.1 · Year 1200, Recall Day 21* [I · World and Campaign](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md) · [II · Areas](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md) · **III · Ways** · [IV · People, Monsters and Treasure](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monsters_and_Treasure.md) ## Contents | Section | Find here | |---|---| | [Travel at the table](#travel) | Turns, encounters, loads, carrying and ascent choices. | | [Service cards](#services) | P passenger; W foot street; F freight; G garden; S water; H household. | | [Restorations and lasting shortcuts](#projects) | Twenty-three projects, with parts, crews, time and cost. | | [Complete Ways](#all-routes) | [DP](#ways-DP) · [ER](#ways-ER) · [FC](#ways-FC) · [GG](#ways-GG) · [LD](#ways-LD) · [LS](#ways-LS) · [RH](#ways-RH) · [RR](#ways-RR) · [RX](#ways-RX) · [SG](#ways-SG) · [SC](#ways-SC). | The Crown's roads run through houses, gardens, walls and empty air. A stair may outlast the neighbourhood it served. A sound cage may hang above a broken drive. Read the visible approach before committing the company and its baggage. ## Travel and passage **One Turn: thirty minutes.** An unfamiliar ordinary approach and locality take one Turn; deliberate investigation adds one. Cross up to three familiar ordinary passages in a Turn, rounding when that continuous run ends. An exceptional journey replaces ordinary movement, followed by one exploration Turn only at an unfamiliar arrival. Rides pass intermediate stops without exploring them. Combat, fuel, spells and treatment retain real minutes. Use [I’s exposure procedure](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#world-procedure): one check per active Turn at the highest risk crossed. Ordinary Ways inherit the greater endpoint risk unless overridden below; exceptional Ways state their rate. Put the event on the approach that supplied the danger. A staffed room can shelter rest while its outer locality remains hazardous. An exceptional Way’s local encounter set takes precedence. Otherwise use travelling results from its endpoint tables whose route and body admit the meeting. Treat the gate’s lair at the gate. Track major patrols by their parent formation and departure; wounded travellers and their carried valuables move together. **Light.** Use the described openings: exterior paths receive daylight, roofed courts their window light, enclosed interiors their stated lamps. At night, unlit stretches are DARK. A dark chamber between two bright landings still needs carried light. Long climbs and mixed routes give local light notes. A torch lasts 60 minutes; one oil fill 240. Opaque walls, corners and shut doors bound illumination. **Access.** Open is the structure’s condition, not a promise of friendly occupants. Doors, secret entrances, damaged links and controls have the means described below. Arrows retain direction. A closed animal route may admit a suitable person or spell; measure the opening and use the movement that fits. **Loads.** Width × lowest headroom; ordinary limits apply to one handled object, cart or litter. A cage or a stated combined-flight limit includes all bodies, gear and load on it. For example, four 75 kg bearers, a 60 kg patient, a 10 kg litter and 40 kg equipment total 410 kg. The patient and litter alone are 70 kg of handled cargo. Use teams and stage movement on limited flights. The named surveyed passages below abbreviate only these identical measurements. An unmeasured “cart/litter access” retains its original fit; inspect unusual loads. | Named passage | Surveyed clearance and load | |---|---| | **Cart gallery** | 2 × 2.3 m; carts and litters; 500 kg handled load. | | **Litter stair** | 1.4 × 2.3 m; packs and carried litter; 100 kg handled cargo. | | **Broad carry** | 2.5 × 2.8 m; packs; 450 kg handled cargo. Litter admission is stated locally. | | **Freight gallery** | 4 × 3.8 m; heavy freight; 8,000 kg handled load. | Tackle, bracing, staged movement and dismantling can solve particular problems. A released bar and completed repair remain useful. The following examples show travel accounting; the event check and fuel follow the time, not the number of dice rolled. | Journey | Turns | |---|---:| | Three familiar passages, then a two-Turn ride to a known landing | 3 | | The same journey to an unfamiliar landing | 4 | | One familiar passage, one-Turn stair, two familiar passages | 3 | | FC001 from known 3 to unfamiliar 1 | 2 | ### Choosing an ascent | At | Direct choice | Other useful country | |---|---|---| | **80 — Exchange Hall** | [FC012](#route-FC012), five-Turn inspection climb to 144: darkness, flood shutter and a rooted upper drain. | The inhabited roofs through **96, 101, 104 and 105** lead toward the gardens, **118** and hospice **132**. Resupply, recruit and learn the next approach. | | **144 — Middle Reserve Water Court** | [FC013](#route-FC013), eight-Turn ascent into 195's occupied north gallery. | Descend by [RX119](#route-RX119) to **135** for [RR205](#route-RR205), which reaches the southern waterkeepers. Hospice **132**, market **128** and [RR196](#route-RR196) lead toward **165** and the crop country. | | **195 — High Cistern Gallery** | [RR206](#route-RR206), seven-Turn inner ascent to refuge **214**. | **194** gives the independent [RR198](#route-RR198) climb to **208**. [P_SUMMIT](#project-P_SUMMIT) creates a permanent one-Turn cage to 208. [FC014](#route-FC014) reaches the occupied king at **206**. | These are visible alternatives to learn through exploration, witnesses and route sketches. The long inspection stairs offer few supplies and expose a returning company to the same doors it passed on the way up. A household chain offers help and information; crop and outer ways expose a different body of hazards. Secured refuges and restored machinery change the next expedition. ![Working service intervals and physical breaks.](maps/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_Service_Intervals.svg) ![Approaches to the highest tower.](maps/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_Highest_Tower_Approach.svg) ## Service cards Crews operate sound banks using local human power. Each failed bank has its own repair below. Joined, repaired banks extend the service; separate working intervals require separate rides and a physical connection between them. A through ride includes loading and transfers inside its continuous working interval. Closed machinery remains an explorable object: its ropes, gates and controls are described under its route ID. For a dormant bank without a listed project, survey the shaft, ropes, brakes, doors and supply first. That survey establishes the parts, skilled crew and working time needed to restore it. ### P — Central Passenger Banks **Working:** **1 ↔ 35 ↔ 47**, at dawn and dusk; **one Turn** per journey. Public passengers, clean packs and handcarts; book a crew for a patient. The sixty-place cage takes **6,500 kg combined live load**; its own counterweighted mass is about 5,000 kg. The upper stops are **74, 128, 165, 195 and 208**, behind independently failed banks. P_LOWER through P_SUMMIT repair them in sections. A continuous restored P interval takes one journey Turn. ### W — West Public Vertical Street **Surviving foot sectors:** **1–35–47–74**, **128–165**, **194–208**. Use each Way's journey time. Breaks lie at **74–128** and **165–194**. People and packs use the stairs; patients need a carrying team. [Rain Stair](#project-RainStair) repairs the second gap. ### F — North Freight Cleft **Working:** **6 ↔ 21 ↔ 29**, by cargo booking; **two Turns** per journey. The cage takes **8,000 kg combined live load**, through a **4 m** loading gate. Passengers travel with the working crew. A cargo bargain, hired work or a patient's transport can obtain a berth. Upper stops **80, 136, 199 and 209** face separate failures. F_LOWER, F_MIDDLE and F_UPPER restore the first three banks; the old transfer to 209 needs its own engineering. A continuous restored F interval takes two journey Turns. ### G — East Garden Cage **Working:** **59 ↔ 99** and, separately, **111 ↔ 118**; **one Turn** within either interval. Growers carry clean crop loads, packs, farm handcarts and patients by agreement. The working cages take **2,000 kg combined live load**. Dirty waste travels by another route. G_PEAR joins the two lower intervals. G_MIDDLE, G_HIGH and G_CLOUD extend passage through **122, 134, 147, 165/166 and 194** as their banks are repaired. The former landings at **158, 176, 186 and 189** remain closed. A continuous restored G journey takes one Turn. ### S — South Water Crew Gallery **Working:** **11 ↔ 41 ↔ 44 ↔ 55 ↔ 73**; **one Turn**. Water crews carry small tools and packs; an accompanying outsider needs their agreement. **500 kg combined live load**, including everyone aboard. S_MIDDLE, S_HIGH and S_SUMMIT restore the separate banks toward **135, 144, 195 and 214**. A continuous restored S journey takes one Turn. ### H — Domestic Terrace Cage **Retired.** The former stops are **54, 58, 64, 70, 96, 101, 105, 143 and 146**. Independent household stairs still carry people and packs. The [H project](#project-H) rebuilds **64 ↔ 96 ↔ 101 ↔ 105**: **one Turn**, **1,500 kg combined live load**, including furniture or a wheeled patient. ## Restorations and lasting shortcuts The prices below are the listed local project outlays. The required parts, people and working time are stated beside them; obtaining distant parts, escorting workers and feeding a remote camp remain expedition tasks. Secure both ends before sending a crew into a shaft. Repairs open the named physical bank. Join it to any adjacent working interval of the same service and record the new usable stops. ### Water — 36 / 202 **Two days · £1 0s 0d (240d).** Replace the lower third-cell gasket and clear the high rejection basket. Two skilled workers need hand tools, a gasket from **26** and the water crew's isolation watch. **Gain:** household water and sample access improve. Fresh make-up demand falls from **580 to 550 m³/day**. ### P_LOWER — 47 / 74 / 29 **Two days · £4 0s 0d (960d).** Lift the caught cage on independent tackle, align its counterweight guides and replace the snapped brake link. Growers’ door. **Passage:** Cart/litter access. ### RX135 — Garden Repair Hoist · [118](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-118) ↔ [121](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-121) Disabled · cage · **1 journey T** · risk 1. The repair hoist waits beside a rack of garden tools. Mud has dried around its platform wheels; the worker doors open onto a silent shaft. Garden workers keep the gates. **Passage:** staff and tools. ### RX136 — Repair Court Field Gate · [121](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-121) ↔ [122](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-122) A growers’ gate opens from the repair court to the East Window headland. Glazing racks and pot barrows follow the short carrying line to the crop porch. **Passage:** Cart/litter access. ### RX137 — Weather Arcade Field Gate · [182](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-182) ↔ [179](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-179) Stone flights descend 50 metres from High Wind House and Weather Arcade to School View East Garden. The weather arcade’s warning bell hangs at the top turn. Below, the renewed teaching enclosure is sheltered by a sound old arch. **Passage:** Packs and carried litter. ### RX138 — Windworks Crew Cage · [193](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-193) ↔ [182](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-182) Disabled · cage · **1 journey T** · risk 3. Windworks tools hang above the dead crew cage. A draught makes the unsecured call plate tap against its box. Windworks crew keep the doors. **Passage:** staff and tools. ### RX139 — North Rigging Approach · [201](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-201) ↔ [202](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-202) The ramp leaves the central rope drums and climbs twenty metres to the north watch porch. Broad roofed turns follow the service wall at about one in twelve; the mesh frames hang outside that wall. Workers’ gate. **Passage:** panel carts and crew. ### RX140 — Northeast Screen Turn · [202](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-202) ↔ [203](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-203) Weather exposed. A roofed cart gallery climbs twenty metres around a stone buttress. Separate wet gutters cross beneath its turns; the ramp averages one in twelve. Rebuilt in Year 4, the screen corner serves rigging crews when wind and mesh tension permit. Workers’ gates. **Passage:** panel carts and crew. ### RX141 — East-to-South Screen Turn · [203](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-203) ↔ [204](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-204) The sunward ramp climbs twenty metres past a viewing recess and the south isolation gate. Broad roofed turning rests hold waiting carts. The grade averages one in twelve along the outer service wall. Workers’ gates. **Passage:** panel carts and crew. ### RX142 — South-to-West Screen Turn · [204](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-204) ↔ [205](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-205) Stone flights rise 20 metres from South Cloud Gallery to West Cloud Gallery. The southern return reaches the western workshop behind masonry screens. Rain-Tongue’s retired outer brace lies beyond a different threshold. **Passage:** people and packs; panel parts carried by crew. ### RX143 — West Repair Return · [205](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-205) ↔ [201](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-201) **1 journey T** · risk 3. The west panel-cart track descends eighty metres past marked furling drums. Roofed runs and broad rests follow the service wall at about one in twelve, ending in the central repair yard. Workers’ gate. **Passage:** panel carts and crew. ### RX144 — Glaziers’ East Screen Door · [199](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-199) ↔ [203](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-203) **1 journey T** · risk 3. Replacement glazing climbs ninety-four metres through roofed ramps along the service wall. Broad turns, about one in twelve, admit the panel frames. The final door opens into the eastern gallery above the wet cistern roofs. Engineers’ gate. **Passage:** panel carts and crew. ### RX145 — East Crop Cage High Continuation · [165](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-165) ↔ [194](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-194) Disabled · cage. From 165, clean crop carts cross the washable [RR223](#route-RR223) transfer to the 166 loading door, then would ride the [RR224](#route-RR224) cage to 194. The missing cable and fallen sheave stop the whole service. [RX145](#route-RX145) is this through itinerary; its cage and lifting limits are [RR224](#route-RR224)'s. **Passage:** Clean farm handcarts, crew and wheeled litter; 2 m wide × 2.3 m high; 2,000 kg combined live load. **Repair:** [G_CLOUD](#project-G_CLOUD). ## SG — Lower garden cage banks [III · Ways index](#all-routes) ### SG001 — Lower Garden Cage · [59](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-59) ↔ [99](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-99) cage · **1 journey T** · risk 3. Screened crop lobbies enclose the lower garden cage. It passes the 66 and 93 shelves without opening, then stops at Pear East’s locked bank-transfer door. Growers load clean farm cargo and arrange space for visitors or patients. The onward [SG002](#route-SG002) bank is disabled. **Passage:** People, packs, clean farm handcarts and wheeled litter; 2 × 2.3 m; 2,000 kg combined live load. ### SG002 — Pear Harvest Transfer · [99](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-99) ↔ [111](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-111) Disabled · cage · **1 journey T** · risk 3. The Pear transfer’s sheave seat is broken and its rope disconnected. Sound enclosed platforms face the stranded cage below its catch. Blue Rill and the inhabited roof terraces offer walking approaches to Harvest Exchange. **Passage:** After G_PEAR repair: people, packs, clean farm handcarts and wheeled litter; 2 × 2.3 m; 2,000 kg combined live load. **Repair:** [G_PEAR](#project-G_PEAR). ## Three hidden returns ### SC001 — The Bell-Rope Return [55 Lower Cistern](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-55) ↔ [57 Tiled Well](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-57) · ordinary; barred, release at 57; risk 2. **Light:** DARK; open endpoint doors admit narrow light. Behind the cistern’s sealed bell-board, a thirty-metre spiral climbs to the old western wash range. The brass lifting ring at 57 draws a stone bar out of the lower door. At 55, tugging the visible cord rings a little bell behind that door but cannot draw the bar. The bar can also be reached with tools through an opened panel; forcing the door is loud ordinary work. **Passage:** 1.2 × 2.3 m; 450 kg handled load. ### SC004 — The Condenser’s Homeward Stair [150 Lantern Refuge](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-150) ↔ [154 Spider Vestibule](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-154) · 1 T; barred, release at 154; risk 3. **Light:** DARK; open endpoint doors admit narrow light. A hundred and fifty metres of enclosed stair follow the cold condenser wall between Lantern’s refuge and the spider-held vestibule. Two tall turns have sound benches for a litter. At 154, an iron handle retracts the heavy lower bar through a visible chain. Its broken inner handle at 150 leaves a tool-sized socket; fitting a replacement or forcing the door is possible from there. The upper door can be shut after passage, excluding pursuing spiders. **Passage:** 1.3 × 2.3 m; 450 kg combined party per flight. ### SC006 — The Observatory Return [198 Bell Refuge](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-198) ↔ [204 South Cloud Walk](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-204) · 1 T; barred, release at 204; risk 3. **Light:** DARK; open endpoint doors admit narrow light. A hundred and fourteen metres of enclosed observation stair connect the refuge’s disused chart closet to the old south instrument platform. Its lower door is held by a lever bar operated at 204 through an intact chain. A crowbar and work at the lower inspection slot can also lift the bar. Two broad half-landings allow a litter to turn. This return bypasses the cargo apron at 199. The upper door can be closed against the wash-duct spider. **Passage:** 1.4 × 2.3 m; 450 kg combined party per flight.

books/THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_IV_People_Monster.text: # IV — PEOPLE, MONSTERS AND TREASURE *THE CROWN · v1.1.1 · Referee's book* [I — World and Campaign](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md) · [II — Areas](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md) · [III — Ways](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_III_Ways.md) ## Contents - [At the table](#table-rules): notation, combat, Wounds, magic and recovery. - [The organism](#organism): invasion, cleansing, centres, [the royal project](#royal-project) and [the Rain](#rain). - [Force ledger](#force-ledger): the opening bodies and their equipment. - [Contacts](#contacts): names, affiliations, locations and profiles. - [People and creatures](#profiles): P01–P47. - [Spell reference](#spells): S01–S19. - [Named items and Sources](#items): the original collection and [selected new wonders](#new-wonders). - [Found equipment](#found-equipment): common weapon, armour and tool interfaces. - [Treasure](#treasures): the complete keyed recoveries. ## At the table The same people, objects, routes and lasting injuries inhabit this GEWINN adventure. The designated GEWINN rules revision is dated 10 October 2026. **Notation.** STR / INT / FTH / WLL are the four Abilities. **DR 11/7/6/5** means Slashing / Piercing / Bludgeoning / Shot; additional protections are named, all unlisted DR is 0. **Move** is feet per combat Move. **ML** is NPC Morale. **Time:** Use [I, expedition procedure](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#world-procedure) for travel, exposure and fuel. **Keep real minutes.** Torch Burn 3 lasts 60 minutes; oil Burn 12 lasts 240. Spend one Burn per 20 minutes alight, including time behind a shutter. Stabilization takes 10 minutes. A 30-minute journey contains three clinical intervals. Safe Rest needs six hours, food, water, adequate shelter and freedom from immediate danger. ### Resolve an uncertain action Check or Save: d20 **under** the Ability; a kept natural 20 fails. Relevant gear gives +1 to the threshold; one real helper gives +1 when help is possible. Opposed rolls use d20 + modifier; the higher wins and the defender wins ties. Ability modifiers: 3–11 +0; 12–13 +1; 14–15 +2; 16–17 +3; 18–19 +4; 20 +5. Damage dice also give initiative: roll and keep them, lower acts first, ties simultaneous. Ordinary Actions use d4; nondamaging spells use d8 per level. Each creature has one Move and one Action. A listed multi-limb routine rolls its attacks separately within that Action. PC attacks use d20 + the appropriate modifier against enemy AC; a PC defending an enemy attack rolls d20 under material AC. Apply matching DR, then Wounds. A muscle weapon with more Damage dice than the user's STR modifier gives one handling [–] per excess die on Attack and Damage. Crossbows and firearms ignore STR handling. Ranged intervals give normal useful range; outside the interval, Attack and Damage each take [–]. Reload occupies the listed number of Actions. A shield takes a hand and contributes only while ready. Count ammunition, smoke, fallen equipment and opened doors when the fight ends. **Control:** d4 Action, opposed STR against the target's STR or WLL. Every helper spending an Action and applying real leverage adds +1. The hold restrains the parts it can reach. Escape uses an Action and the same opposed roll. A declared melee Finisher automatically hits a still-Controlled target and ignores physical DR; release before resolution spoils the Finisher. Shield Sacrifice spends one condition step to reduce the incoming severity once before accumulation. **Reaction and Morale.** When disposition is uncertain, 2d6: 2 or less conflict; 3–5 hostile; 6–8 uncertain; 9–11 favourable; 12 or more helpful. NPCs test 2d6 when the decision to stand is uncertain; a result over ML breaks them. PCs use their own d20 Morale Saves. Each failed player-facing roll costs 1 Morale and gives 1 Stress; a failed Morale Save also supplies the Panic result. Real relief and downtime use the core procedures. ### Wounds once, injuries in their place Ordinary NPCs and creatures accumulate **one WV across all damage types**, after the correct DR has been applied to each hit. Describe the injured limb or organ. Profiles explicitly marked **Great** use typed Wounds like PCs. **Huge** subtracts its listed WV reduction after DR on bodily hits, including magic. Keep each creature's current injuries when it changes rooms or retreats. | Accumulated WV | Severity | Immediate consequence | |---:|---|---| | 1–3 | Minor | Mark the injury. | | 4–6 | Serious | WLL Save or lose an unresolved Action. | | 7–9 | Grave | Lose an unresolved Action; WLL Save or Out; 1d4 Ability Loss on entering this band. | | 10–15 | Mortal | As Grave; a further 1d4 Ability Loss on first entering Mortal. Mortal Die = 16 − WV. | | 16+ | Catastrophic | Death or irreversible destruction as the actual injury dictates. | An unstabilized Grave injury tests WLL every 10 real minutes; failure adds 1 WV. A Mortal Die decreases at each later 10-minute interval while unstabilized or active. In combat, an injured person's later Action or Move reduces it once that Round. Stabilized rest or careful carrying holds the die. Further injury and exertion still matter. A lethal injury to an exposed vital part follows the anatomy in its profile. ### Magic and Sources INT and FTH have separate Memory capacities, each equal to its modifier in total spell levels. Copies are individual: two level-1 copies fill Memory 2. Where a standard spell scales by caster level, use the governing modifier, **minimum 1**. Cast through one Attack, one appropriate Defense or an automatic effect. Spell use is spent when initiative or Damage is rolled, even if interrupted. Physical Source access lets a character learn in **one day per spell level** and restore one spent copy in **one hour per level**, unless that Source names a different service or time. Complete copies require the actual text, work and materials. Standard The two original Crown observances, S11 and S12, are printed in full below. **Sacrifice:** a d4 Action restores one exact spent copy. The caster receives Recharge WV **3 / 6 / 9 / 15 / 16** for levels 1–5, of the spell's listed type. DR, magical healing and transfer leave that sacrifice in place; natural recovery follows the core. **Artifices:** INT governs Attack and handling. Each Damage die above the INT modifier adds one [–]. A ranged discharge reloads in as many Actions as it has Damage dice; GEWINN Artifices use this reload cycle. Melee use remains available during Reload and leaves the reload unfinished. **Relics:** rated NdS of a damage type. Possession gives personal DR equal to **S**. Once per Safe Rest, spend an Action and touch one willing recipient: roll NdS for their flat Bestowed DR until their Safe Rest. Each die above the FTH modifier adds [–]; the modifier itself adds no points. Add the highest personal protection, highest Bestowed protection and any applicable ordinary protection. Repeated Relics of the same kind use those best values. ### Taking things home **Money:** £1 = 20s = 240d; 1s = 12d. **Load:** one Slot is about three pounds; £10 0s 0d (2,400d) in ordinary coin weighs one Slot. Treasure loads include their cases and packing where stated. Maximum Load is 2 × STR Slots; ready Move is 40 + 5 × STR modifier, less 5 feet per complete five carried Slots. Use a creature's printed natural Move where its anatomy supplies a different rate. **Condition:** Sound → Worn → Ruined. Worn equipment works; repair it during Safe Rest with tools. Ruined pieces require appropriate workshop work or replacement. Clean and fit recovered armour by component; a chest's bundled Slots describe carrying it, while the pieces describe wearing it. Appraisal records useful sale value; a buyer's offer, a purchase cost and a promised reward are separate sums. The treasure cards identify money mixed with magic. Existing owners, bargains and actual sale conditions belong to the encounter. **Corpse pockets:** roll d12 once for an intact ordinary corpse, twice for an officer or wealthy person. Carried armour and weapons are additional. Record the result so later searches find the same objects. | d12 | Pocket or pack | |---:|---| | 1 | Purse: 1d6 shillings, 12d per point rolled. | | 2 | Heavy purse: 2d6 shillings, 12d per point. | | 3 | 1d6 actual shots of ammunition. | | 4 | Rope, lantern, rations, spikes or water. | | 5 | One tool suited to the person's work. | | 6 | 1d3 clean dressings. | | 7 | Jewellery worth 1d6 shillings, 12d per point. | | 8 | Badge worth 1d4 shillings, 12d per point. | | 9 | Letters or paybook identifying a person, debt or appointment. | | 10 | Gem or watch worth 2d6 shillings, 12d per point. | | 11 | An actual route clue consistent with the person's journey. | | 12 | Portable goods worth £1 plus 2d6 shillings: 240d + 12d per point. | ## The organism The Necromancer is an ancient intelligence living through fungal tissue, larvae and occupied hosts. Animated corpses are **Dead and undead**: they ignore Bleeding, suffocation, ordinary biological poison, Sleep and Charm Person. A person under invasion remains **Living** until nerve replacement destroys them. Larvae are supernatural vermin. The three porcelain Collectors are **Made** machines. Apply a defense to the kind of body actually present. ### Reach and timing Warnings and speech pass immediately along connected roots and ganglia. Bodies and messengers travel through the Ways. A severed link leaves a group carrying out its last order, then reacting to local sight, sound and contact. The organism learns an unrooted neighbour's affairs by sending something there. | Process | What must be present | Time and result | |---|---|---| | Secure a corpse | Actual accessible dead body | One d4 Action threads it. | | Establish infestation | Continued access to the body | 30 minutes makes it Infested. | | Ordinary maturation | Infested body, water, biomass and a curing place | A further 60 minutes makes a lasting mature body. | | Warm trays at 156 | Supplied, rooted N02 and an already-Infested corpse | 15 minutes per body, maximum two per 30 minutes. | | Force the Dead | P08 or P42 and a reachable Secured or Infested corpse | A separate d4 Action; P09 rises next Round and lasts 30 real minutes. | | Proximity Bloom | Fresh eligible death in P08's encounter and local access | Rises in 1d4 Rounds, retaining its actual body and equipment. | Guarding, removal, sealed containment, meaningful washing or salt, fire and dismemberment can deny access. Apply the method to the tissue and corpse it reaches. Secured stock waits for further work or an actual Force Action. ### A living casualty Start a written clock when a hand-sized colony enters an **open Grave or worse Wound**, or reaches a helpless dying casualty. Covered wounds, movement, conscious resistance and prompt treatment can prevent the required access. Nearby roots alone require ordinary care in choosing a path. 1. **Continued wound exposure:** 1 Toxic Damage every 30 minutes, matching DR applies. 2. **After 30 uninterrupted helpless minutes:** peripheral nerves are reached. The Living Invaded host can be moved by the parasite, using its real anatomy, equipment and one Action. 3. **After a further 60 uninterrupted helpless minutes, 90 total:** white spinal and brain cords replace the nervous tissue. The person is dead; the body becomes mature Dead. Moving a casualty out of danger gives the rescuers room to work; an internal colony still needs removal. Tell an examiner the elapsed stage and show its signs: fibres in the wound, involuntary movement, whitening cords, lost responses. Wounds and Ability Loss survive a successful rescue. **Intervene now.** One Action with salt, washing or reaching tools clears a hand-sized surface patch. Deep cleansing needs **10 minutes**, light, clean water, instruments, access and a helper. Competent work with adequate means succeeds. Under pressure or with poor tools, use an INT Check with actual Gear and Aid; failure spends ten minutes and adds 1 Piercing WV. Stabilize other injuries independently. Fire inside a wound burns the patient too. Before the 90-minute boundary, successful cleansing, [Cure Disease](#spell-S13) or a [Cleansing draught](#item-M15) removes the parasites. Trained surgery can reach invaded nerves where the anatomy and tools permit. After the brain and spinal tissue are replaced, ordinary healing cannot reconstruct the lost person. The [royal project](#royal-project) requires preserving Odelia Marr's living brain and obtaining her deliberate, learned command. ### Countermeasures **Turning:** a suitable Source or Authority, one Action, FTH Check. Success drives off 2d6 total HD; each affected undead must have HD no greater than the FTH modifier. Raw corpses P09 are 1 HD; P10 and P46 are 2; P11 is 4; P47 is 5; P08 is 12. Larvae and Made cores use other countermeasures. A sacred funeral bell forces one exposed Raw or larval group to test Morale at each new acoustic contact. Blessed water and sacred washing destroy exposed larvae they reach and cause **1d8 Burning-equivalent damage** to contacted dead infested tissue; armour and masonry can keep the water outside. Protection from Evil bars enchanted host hands and larvae from melee contact until its subject attacks. An internal colony already touching its host needs cleansing. Dispel Magic ends a sustained spell or magical control that is actually targeted. Remove Curse can break a recognised possession binding with access. Physical organisms, their nerve tissue and ancient machine cores remain available for the treatment or damage appropriate to them. ### Centres and lasting defeat **Exposed feeder knots, N01–N04:** stationary, GEWINN AC 0; DR 4/6/0/2, Burning 0, Toxic 12, Freezing 8. One Grave or worse Wound disables the knot. Prepared heavy cutting, quicklime, directed hot water or draining the centre's own work-water can succeed with adequate access and means. | Centre | Where to reach it | What its loss removes | |---|---|---| | N01 — lower ganglion | Two-metre knot around the pump at 99 | Lower remote feeding and coordination. The crop main is separate. | | N02 — curing house | Trays and feed trunks at 156 | Fifteen-minute rapid maturation. Ordinary curing still takes an hour. | | N03 — warning link | North gallery at 195; three frame clamps or its separate water jacket | Instant communication between upper and lower tissue. | | N04 — grafting work | Corpse-stock feed trunks at 206 | Sophisticated replacement bodies. | | N05 — Heart | 207; [P42](#profile-P42) gives cover and lethal access | Central coordination and every return mechanism. | An isolated king-body retains its nearby jet, touch, Majesty, Force and Bloom; distant speech, information and withdrawal depend on a connected route. With the Heart alive but grafting at 206 destroyed, it can occupy a connected existing body after **2d6 weeks**. Prepared replacement uses real corpse stock and the surviving work at 206; keep its work and route on the campaign record. **Permanent defeat:** kill the Heart, defeat the surviving sophisticated bodies, and kill or physically seal the visible final brain-squid [P43](#profile-P43). Heart death makes every remaining manifestation permanently mortal. Local larvae can still infest a wound and physically direct a nearby host, but have lost the central intelligence. Rescued people, severed centres and destroyed bodies remain changed. ### The royal project The Necromancer wants a living royal bearer who can deliberately command the Motive. Odelia Marr has the inheritance; she must still learn its use. The parasite uses threats, a stolen father's tenderness and promises about other captives to obtain purposeful cooperation. Keep a dated project note with these requirements: 1. **A living, conscious Odelia Marr.** Record where she is held, her condition, her guards and what she has learned. 2. **Access to the hand hollows at 215.** Establish a usable route from 217 and the bodies needed to move and guard her. The dismantled Signal Stair requires work. 3. **Instruction.** Obtain a knowledgeable living tutor, usable charts or observed successful commands. Record the particular command being learned and its conditions. 4. **For the neural graft:** retain the stock at 206, the signal centre at 195, a knowledgeable living attendant and the restrained princess for **14 uninterrupted days of preparation**. The fourth requirement begins a specific prepared attempt. Missing or interrupted requirements stop that attempt; restart its preparation when the necessary people, centres and equipment are again assembled. Threats and ordinary coercion can proceed while the fine work is blocked. **Opening status, Recall Day 21:** the fourteen-day preparation has yet to begin. Odelia Marr has learned no command, the Signal Stair is broken, and the captors still seek the required instruction. The stock and centres are ready below. Date the first day when the princess, skilled attendant and complete preparation are assembled; record each interruption thereafter. **At the table.** Each completed day leaves evidence: a requested instrument, clean linen sent upward, a new restraint, a tutor's disappearance, or practice marks at the controls. Give the company the evidence where its contacts and position allow. A prisoner can smuggle an appeal or bargain for the release of another captive. For the graft itself, use the living-invasion times above. Peripheral control begins after thirty uninterrupted helpless minutes. Retaining the royal faculties requires waking and stabilising Odelia Marr before the following sixty minutes destroy her person. An awake invaded princess still needs instruction and must form the command herself. Her wounds, fear, resistance and opportunities to communicate remain in play. Rescue, cleansing or the loss of skilled attendants can defeat the attempt at its stage. Odelia Marr’s character, transformation and possible future appear in [I — The royal inheritance](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_I_World_and_Campaign.md#world-royal). ### The Rain The Rain is a human gravity-bombardment work: **207 stores and transfers ammunition; 206 loads the fall well; 8 holds its lower shutters and inspection interlocks**. The great tube runs between them. Pedestrians use the separate inspection landings and cage. At the opening, the cradles are empty, the magazine houses the heart, the inspection cage lacks power, and the ventral shutters are dogged shut above Marrbridge. The parasite holds the upper works; two Crown Watch scouts hold the lower inspection landing. To prepare a discharge, establish the following in order: | Requirement | Physical action and warning | |---|---| | **A target beneath the aperture** | Observe the ground from the lower works. Repositioning the Crown requires a learned royal command and a suitable hold; wind and the moving ground remain visible to observers. | | **Actual ammunition** | Obtain a load, bring it along a route that bears its weight, and store it behind the magazine partitions. Imported powder, shells or other burdens appear on the carrying account. | | **Working handling gear** | Clear the rail and loading space, provide the human machinery's power, and repair its failed parts. Hand tackle can move only the burden its crew and anchors can support. Tools, drive noise and traffic reveal the work. | | **An open fall well** | Inspect the tube and interlocks, secure exposed inspection positions, and release the shutter dogs at 8. The lower crew can bar, disable or contest them. Dust, moving dogs and a widening shaft of daylight give warning below. | | **A crew at the release** | Load at 206, confirm the lower shutter and operate the mechanical release. Resolve the falling burden and impact in its path. Each further load needs its own handling. | Record the materials, workers, routes and completion times as an expedition project. Progress requires all of them. A liberated attendant can explain a bar; a raiding company can remove ammunition, wreck tackle, seize the interlocks or evacuate the ground below. The Crown continues to fly after the parasite is killed; its surviving works belong to those who can reach and use them. ## Force ledger **Recall Day 21: 160 mature bodies — 112 human and 48 animal.** Origins: 32 royal dead, 16 recently killed residents, 64 old human bodies and 48 animals. The twelve bodies taken from 39 are already in the old-human total. The occupied king and three Collectors are separate. Twenty-four secured royal corpses await work or Force; they are included among the seventy-one royal dead still unmatured. Twelve larval colonies complete the opening stock. | Locality | Human bodies | Animal bodies | Deployment and equipment | |---|---|---|---| | [99](THE_CROWN_v1_1_1_II_Areas.md#node-99) | 18 P10 | — | Eight at the gate; ten on feeding racks. GEWINN
Old School Renaissance Fantasy
  
 
 
Copyright and Attribution
Gewinn: Old School Renaissance Fantasy - Tabletop RPG

Art and Illustrations
	Predica del arte del bene morire (Sermon on the Art of Dying Well) by Girolamo Savonarola, 1502.
	Der Weisskunig 109 Landsknecht Battle by Hans Burgkmair, 1516.
	Danse Macabre (16, 19, 27, 31, 42) by Hans Holbein, 1493.
	Wound Man from Hans von Gersdorff's Feldtbuch der Wundartzney, 1519.
	Arkebusier, Nbg.1 kl

Acknowledgments

This project has been made possible thanks to the contributions of many creators and the open-source gaming community. All rules, tables, and artwork are inspired by or derived from the classic traditions of tabletop role-playing games and medieval art.
Credit to cavegirlgames for the “Horrible Wounds” system and Mothership for the “Stress” system.
Published by: Marshall Alexander, 2024 — Updated October  10th, 2026
Disclaimer: This work is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. The publisher shall not be held liable for any damages resulting from the use of this material.
Contact: Kosmosius@protonmail.com
  
 
Gewinn
Gewinn is Hael, and Hael ne æfre ceorfað hwæt ælc man mid eagan on his hēafde wiste, þæt Gewinn toweard wæs; Winnan, Giefu, and Gewinn.
War is Hell, and Hell never changed what any man with eyes in his head knew when war was at hand; Conflict, Gain, and Profit.
WHAT IS GEWINN?
GEWINN is an old-school fantasy adventure game where violence and wonder are material: steel, cloth, plate, powder, fire, frost, poison, mud, hunger, light, wounds, debt, witnesses, rank, law, property, and time.
It is classless and level-less. Characters are defined by four Abilities, what they possess, whom they know and owe, and what they survive. Armour provides AC and typed DR; Damage that gets through becomes persistent, accumulating Wounds. Failed rolls become Stress. Wealth becomes equipment, influence, property, Revelry, and Growth.
Characters begin with a debt-free Loadout and may take the Deal for leveraged equipment, recording a creditor, principal, and terms.
Magic is also property. Spells require Sources; miracles require sacred Sources or Authority. Books, relics, shrines, names, offices, teachers, instruments, and secrets may be owned, borrowed, licensed, inherited, stolen, damaged, forbidden, or fought over.
GEWINN is a game of hard choices, lasting injury, and dangerous magic.
THE GAME
Players equip expeditions, enter dangerous places, gather information, manage time and supplies, negotiate, avoid or confront danger, carry wealth home, recover, and return changed.
Scouting, preparation, tools, allies, reaction, morale, retreat, and judgment matter more than winning fair fights. Violence leaves consequences. Light burns. Powder smokes. Gear wears. Treasure occupies Slots. Wounds persist. Witnesses remember. Debts come due.
THE EXPEDITION
PREPARE → ENTER → EXPLORE → LEARN → DECIDE → RISK → SURVIVE → RETURN → REVEL → GROW
At the entrance, time and light seem plentiful. Deeper in, every search, detour, fight, wound, and heavy prize consumes part of the way home. Success means returning with something worth the cost.
How To PLAY
THE FLOW
The Dungeon Master describes the world, what is perceptible, and what its people and powers do. Players ask questions and describe what their characters attempt. Play moves between description, decisions, established procedures, and rolls when the outcome remains uncertain and consequential. 
For a consequential action:
1.	State intent and method. Say what you want and how you do it.
2.	Consult the fiction. Consider position, time, tools, knowledge, opposition, and consequences.
3.	Resolve. If the method makes the result certain, it happens. If an established procedure applies, use it. Otherwise, when the result remains uncertain and consequential, state what is at risk and roll.
4.	Apply the result. The world changes; new circumstances may make the next action easier, harder, possible, or unnecessary.
CORE RESOLUTION
Dice: NdX means roll N dice with X sides and add them.
Checks & Saves: Roll 1d20 under the relevant Ability. A kept natural 20 always fails.
Opposed Rolls: Both sides roll 1d20 + relevant Ability modifier. Higher wins; ties favour the defender or existing state.
Advantage [+] / Disadvantage [–]. Each independent advantage grants [+]; each independent disadvantage grants [–]. Opposing edges cancel one-for-one. After cancellation, roll the procedure once plus once for each remaining edge and keep the most or least favourable complete result. Thus [+] rolls twice, [++] three times, and [+++] four times; [-], [– –], and [– – –] work likewise. Only the kept result counts, including natural results. For Damage, higher is favourable.
Every failed player-facing roll causes Morale –1 / Stress +1. Morale and Stress share one twenty-point track. When terror or calamity tests nerve, make a Morale Save; failure also determines Panic.
VIOLENCE
When immediate physical jeopardy begins, shift to Combat Rounds.
At the start of each round, declare an action and roll its dice. A damaging action rolls its Damage Dice. That total is initiative: lower acts first; ties are simultaneous. If the attack lands, retain the same total as Damage. Ordinary Actions roll 1d4; non-damaging spells and miracles roll 1d8 per level.
Player Attack: d20 + relevant modifier ≥ enemy AC
Enemy Attack: The Dungeon Master rolls Damage; the player rolls d20 under current AC to avoid it.
When an attack lands: Wound Value = Damage – matching DR
At 0 or less, the attack is Stopped. At 1 or more, read the result on the matching Wound Table. Wounds of the same damage type accumulate. Armour buys time, not immortality. Combat ends when violence ends. Return to exploration time and account for wounds, light, ammunition, Reload, damaged or dropped gear, smoke, noise, Stress, witnesses, pursuit, and changed load.
MAGIC
A spell or miracle uses one resolution: caster Attack, target Defense, or no roll—never both. Remembered magic is learned and restored through a Source or Authority, but may be used away from it. Spent magic returns only through its required study, prayer, rite, or observance; ordinary sleep restores nothing. Sacrifice may restore magic immediately by accepting a Wound.
GROWTH
GEWINN has no experience levels. During downtime, characters turn accumulated Stress and wealth into Growth through Revelry, raising the Abilities their lives have tested.
 
  
 
Philosophy
THE WORLD IS WORTH ENGAGING 
GEWINN is a game about ordinary, unchosen people becoming consequential in a world that does not revolve around them.
It is a materially serious and genuinely enchanted world. Steel has weight. Money has value. Wounds, weather, law, labor, reputation, and debt shape what a person can do. The dead may return, relics may answer faith, and something beneath the hill may be older than its stones.
It is an old world, but not a finished one. A person’s place is real, but not final. No class defines what you may become, and no level makes the world yield before you. Your character is a history: the craft learned, wound endured, debt paid, oath broken, friendship earned, property acquired, and name made.
You become what you do.
No one makes themselves alone or is only what they inherited. Freedom is not isolation from every obligation, but the growing power to choose your obligations, refuse ruinous terms, protect what you love, and act without living wholly at another’s mercy. Skill, knowledge, friendship, wealth, reputation, and a place of your own enlarge that power; each also brings duties, risks, and attention.
GEWINN is dangerous because consequences are real, not because the game wishes to punish you. It is hopeful because agency is real, not because the game promises to save you. The world will not arrange itself for your victory. Neither will it conspire to deny you one.
The world does not promise that you will win. It promises that winning is possible.
HOW TO READ THESE RULES
The concrete precedes the abstract. Things are first what they are in the world. Rules describe them; they do not replace them.
The world precedes the character sheet. Look outward before looking down. The sheet records possibilities, but does not contain them all.
Circumstances determine the roll. Dice resolve meaningful uncertainty; they do not manufacture it. Change the circumstances and you change the roll.
Power has a bearer. Someone owns the gate, holds the debt, commands the watch, knows the road, or speaks for the village. Find where power resides and how it acts.
Consequences are the substance of play. Wounds, wealth, knowledge, loyalties, enemies, obligations, and property change what becomes possible next.
Wonder belongs to the world. The ordinary gives the extraordinary its power. The fantastic exists alongside gunpowder, commerce, inheritance, craftsmanship, and hunger; it has signs, causes, limits, and consequences even when unknown.
The rules face the players; the world does not. Players roll most dice so choice and risk remain visible, not because their characters are privileged. People, monsters, weather, distance, and time follow the same logic without them.
Abstraction preserves consequence. A Slot, Turn, Wound, or Reaction roll compresses reality so the table can act. Use the simplest rule that preserves the important choice; add detail only when it changes what someone can know or do.
Scale remains real. Strength, wealth, tools, followers, office, and magic enlarge what a person can accomplish; greater tasks still require greater means. Do not reduce every obstacle to one personal roll.

FOR THE PLAYERS
Engage with the world. Ask questions, examine things, speak to people, test assumptions, seek leverage, and change the situation before risking yourself. Do not search only your character sheet for permission to act.
Learn before you risk. Warnings, customs, tracks, rumors, old books, and strange precautions may contain useful truth. The unknown is not unknowable.
Treat danger as real and make fights unfair. Ambush, bargain, outnumber, deceive, trap, research, prepare, retreat, or return at daylight. Combat is one possible consequence of your decisions, not their required conclusion.
Choose what you owe. Other people make possible what solitary ability cannot, but every durable relationship establishes expectations. Know the terms, repay generosity, notice when assistance becomes control, and seek the means to walk away.
Treat wealth as capacity. Money buys tools, labor, information, property, influence, independence, and time. Gain matters because it lets you do what you could not do before.
Become what you do. Practice a craft, earn trust, acquire property, protect a household, repair what was ruined, or build something that outlives you. Decide what winning means, what it is worth, and when you have gained enough to leave.
FOR THE Dungeon Master
Portray a world, not a plot. Ask what is here, what has happened, what each party wants, and what will occur without interference. Then allow the characters to interfere.
The world need not be fair; you must be. Telegraph perceptible danger, preserve consequences, let good plans work, and never alter the world merely to rescue, punish, or obstruct the players.
Give information generously and certainty sparingly. Meaningful choice requires evidence, but evidence need not provide complete understanding.
Give power a purpose, a bearer, a cost, and a limit. People and institutions should do real things. Authority should be concrete enough to bargain with and limited enough to resist.
Let plans change reality. A barred door is harder to open. A bribed guard may look away. A creature lured into daylight stands in daylight. Resolve the action proposed, not merely the nearest named mechanic.
Keep the supernatural strange, but never arbitrary. Give it patterns, appetites, limits, histories, and signs. Mystery should reward investigation, not change its nature solely to defeat the players.
Let the world remember, and do not erase success. Debts come due, survivors speak, roads reopen, and mercy may return years later. Wealth should solve problems money can solve. Knowledge should remain true. Gains may bring new dangers, but they must remain gains.
Do not confuse misery with seriousness. Permit comfort, loyalty, celebration, prosperity, beauty, and peace. These are not interruptions to adventure; they are reasons adventure matters.
Allow the characters to become consequential. Let them acquire property, followers, enemies, offices, dependents, institutions, and legacies. If they change the world, the world afterward should be different.
The world may be harsh, but it is not empty. It may be unjust, but action is not futile. Human beings can still learn, create, prosper, repair, protect, and build.
GEWINN is not a game about escaping the world. It is a game about entering it, taking it seriously, and making something of yourself within it.
Nothing guarantees victory.
But victory is real.
 


 
 
 
Character CREATION
Roll your Wound. Assign your abilities. Take the Deal—or don’t.
Loadouts
A Loadout is equipment and circumstance, not a class. It tells what you possess and where you came from, not what you are good at or what you become. Each is anchored by the weapon, artifice, or relic shown on the facing Wound Man. Values differ; ownership does not imply skill. The anchor and all bold Debt-Free equipment are owned outright.
Create a Character
1.	Roll 1d20 on the Wound Man, or choose 0. Custom.
2.	Roll 3d6 four times; assign the scores among STR, INT, FTH, and WLL.
3.	Take the Loadout’s bold Debt-Free equipment.
4.	If it grants Source Access and you have Memory, choose or roll one appropriate Level-1 spell or miracle.
5.	Take the Deal—or don’t. Add the Leveraged equipment and its listed Debt.
6.	Record Creditor—Principal—Terms.
7.	Roll 1d6s + 1d12d pocket money.
8.	Record Morale 20 / Stress 0, AC, DR, Slots, Maximum Load, and Move; name the character.
Starting equipment cannot be sold or exchanged during creation. In play, dispose of it as you wish—and answer to any claimant. If overloaded, cache, mount, or redistribute enough gear to travel.
Expedition Kit
Every Loadout includes: Backpack or haversack, small sack, flint & steel, 2 days’ rations, full waterskin; 4 Slots · 1s 3d
This kit is included in all listed Slots and values.
Source Access
Some Loadouts grant Spell L1 or Sacred L1 Source Access. You know and may return to an appropriate teacher, library, laboratory, shrine, monastery, collection, patron, or other Source, but do not own it.
With at least INT +1 or FTH +1, respectively, choose or roll one appropriate Level-1 spell or miracle to begin remembered. At +0, you retain Access but remember nothing until your modifier rises. Access has no Slots or resale value; a listed Arcane or Holy Book is an owned Source.
Take the Deal
Leveraged equipment is optional. Its listed Debt is the principal financed, not a universal repayment formula. Record the creditor and terms: coin, interest, service, loyalty, collateral, information, treasure, protection, or return of property.
When a Deal says replace, exchange the Debt-Free item for the financed one; do not keep both. Debt is a relationship, and creditors act through the world.
0. Custom
Take the Expedition Kit and £1 to spend on ordinary Standard equipment. Choose one item as your anchor. You may spend 1s of the allowance for Arcane or Sacred L1 Source Access. Finance anything more through Debt. Restricted, Elite, and Unique property still requires an appropriate patron, institution, creditor, theft, inheritance, or other explanation.
